solution: (A) 우리의 조상인 호모 사피엔스들이 궁극적으로 살아남고 번 영했다고 했으므로 어떻게 우리는 그렇게 오랫동안 ‘살아남을’ 수 있었는지를 묻는 것이 자연스럽다. 따라서 survive(살아남다)가 알맞다. (B) 네안데르탈인들이 잘 발달된 근육과 넓은 어깨를 가진 튼 튼한 신체를 가지고 있었다는 설명이 나오고, 이러한 특성에도 불구하고 호모 사피엔스가 살아남았다고 했으므로 호모 사피 엔스보다 네안데르탈인들의 신체적 조건이 ‘우월했’다가 흐름 상 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘superior(더 우수한)’가 알맞다. (C) 호모 사피엔스들이 협력하고 지식의 자유로운 교환을 촉진 하는 더 큰 공동체를 이룬 것이 그들이 생존에 유리한 이점이 되었을 것이라고 설명하고 있으므로 그러한 사회적 특성이 끊 임없이 변화하는 환경에 ‘적응하도록’ 했다는 흐름이 자연스럽 다. 따라서 adapt to ~(~에 적응하다)가 알맞다.

In our ⓐcompetitive society, many people believe
that only the biggest or the strongest can survive
and thrive. However, I propose an ⓑalternative
view: kindness is the key to success. Isn’t that a
comforting thought? We can use the power of our
natural kindness to communicate and cooperate

this instead of trying to be better than others. I’d

I’ll give you another example of how friendliness is

designed an experiment with chimpanzees and
bonobos. Although the two are genetically similar,
they
are
different
in
nature.

their

team set up a device which required two individuals
to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in
order to access food on a board. When placed with
partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were
(B)[unable / able] to work together to get the food.
However, when paired with new partners, the
chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and
when they occasionally succeeded, they did not
share the food with their partner. The bonobos, on
the other hand, got along much better than the
chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of
which individual they were paired with, and they
were also more (C)[reluctant / willing] to share the
food. This research shows that bonobos have a
cooperative and friendly nature. Experts suggest that
their nature has helped their species survive.
Without these characteristics, they could have faced
extinction.

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 표현으로알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: you were intrigued by science fiction
you were fascinated by science fiction

you were concerned about science fiction
solution: 밑줄 친 (A)는 ‘네가 공상 과학 소설에 관심이 있었는지’의 의 미로, ‘be동사+interested in ~'는 ’~에 관심이 있다‘는 뜻을 가 지며 어떤 것에 대한 흥미나 관심이 있음을 나타낼 때 사용된 다. 그러나 ❺ ’너는 공상 과학 소설에 대해 걱정했는지‘의 의 미이므로 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 없다. 참고로, 흥미, 관심을 나타내는 표현으로 ’be동사+into ~(~에 푹 빠지다), be동사+fascinated by ~(~에 매료되다), be동사 +curious about ~(~에 호기심이 있다), be동사+intrigued by ~(~에 강한 흥미를 느꼈다) 등이 있다.

body:
For some time, ⓐmy grandfather had been busy
writing down the village genealogy, knowing as the
whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old
house. But then came the night of the fire, which
ran through the house and (A)[destroyed / glorified]
our past. In only one night, everything we knew
was gone. Nani Tama, in (B)[despair / hope], went
to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina.
Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past,
Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his
shaky hands. He chanted the names of the ancestors,
(C)[joining / attributing] the past to the present
once more. The village went quiet and listened to
his chanting. ⓑHis voice traveled along the lines of
our genealogy, searched back across the centuries.
Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to
remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the
middle of the chant. The village waited in worried
silence until the next name burst out of his mouth.
It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most
of the whakapapa, but there were still missing
names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to
drive him to Murupara to finish his work.

ⓑ symbolic: having a meaning that is exactly asstated; being literal
ⓒ accomplishments: things that someone has successfullydone or achieved through effort

solution: symbolic은 ‘상징적인’이란 의미이므로 ⓑ ‘상징적인: 말 그대로 의 의미를 가지는; 문자 그대로의 의미인’이라는 영영풀이는 어 색하다. 대신, ‘representing something else, especially an idea or a meaning; rather than being literal(다른 것을, 특히 어떤 아이디어나 의미를 나타내는; 문자 그대로의 의미가 아닌)’으로 풀이되는 것이 알맞다. ⓐ 전통적인: 오랫동안 존재해왔으며, 세대에서 세대로 전해지 는 것을 따르는 ⓒ 성취: 사람이 노력하여 성공적으로 해낸 일이나 성취한 것들 ⓓ 신성한: 종종 종교나 전통과 관련된, 신성하게 여겨지며 존 중받을 만한 ⓔ 보존하다: 어떤 것을 원래 상태로 유지하거나 손상이나 변 화로부터 보호하다

like she’s making fun of someone.
B: I know, it does look like that, but she’s actually
just saying hi. In certain regions of Tibet, sticking
out tongues like that is a traditional way of
greeting people.
G: Really? So, it’s like waving our hands or giving a
high-five?
B: Yes, exactly! There’s an interesting history behind
why Tibetans do it.
G: Oh, yeah? What’s that?
B: Well, it’s said that there was a cold-blooded king
named Lang Darma, who had a black tongue. To
prove they weren’t related to him, Tibetans started
showing their tongues when they met someone new.
G: Oh, interesting. But isn’t sticking out tongues
considered a bit rude in some cultures, like ours?
B: That’s true, but not in Tibet. So, if you ever visit
Tibet, (A)make sure not to get offended when
someone sticks their tongue out at you!

ensure that you don't get offended
be careful not to get offended
solution: 밑줄 친 (A)는 ‘기분 나빠하지 마라’의 의미로, ‘~하지 않도록 조심해라’는 의미로 주의를 당부하는 표현인 ‘make sure not+to부정사’가 쓰였다. 그러나 ❺는 '기분이 상하지 않는 것 을 피하라‘의 의미로 이중 부정이 되어 다른 의미가 된다. 따 라서 avoid getting offended로 고쳐야 유사한 의미를 갖는다.

body:
It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather
most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing
names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to
drive him to Murupara to finish his work.
When I arrived at Auntie’s place, I was shocked to
see how thin Nani Tama was. “Look, Nani,” I said.
“I’m not taking you anywhere. You could die on
me!” Nani looked at me in anger. “You want me to
die here in this room? Looking at these four walls?
When the whakapapa is (A)___________________?”
The old man held on tightly to the side of the
bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow,
painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could
not help but carry him to the car, and we set off
with Auntie.
We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to
Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but
wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he burst into a
song that he had taught Auntie. They sang
together, lifting up their voices to send the song
flying like a bird through the sky.

solution: (A) 타 모코가 개인의 족보나 사회적 지위, 개인적인 성취에 대 한 것들을 각각의 구부러진 선과 모양으로 나타낸다고 했으므 로 그러한 문신의 선과 모양이 개인의 여정에 대한 symbolic (상징적인) 의미를 가진다는 흐름이 알맞다. (B) 타 모코의 각각의 구부러진 선과 모양이 개인의 족보, 사회 적 지위, 개인적인 성취를 나타낸다고 했을 뿐만 아니라 뒤에 나이가 들수록 삶의 경험을 나타내기 위해 더 많은 선과 모양 을 문신에 더한다는 내용이 이어지므로, 개인마다 다른 디자인 의 타 모코를 가지고 있음을 알 수 있다. 따라서 어떤 타 모코 디자인도 ‘같지’ 않다는 흐름이 되어야 하므로 the same(같은) 이 오는 것이 흐름상 알맞다. (C) 전통적인 마오리족의 문신 예술인 타 모코가 요즘 덜 흔하 기는 하지만 마오리 족 사람들에 의해 오늘날에도 여전히 행 해지고 있으며, 이렇게 여전히 타 모코를 행하는 사람들은 그 들의 전통과 유산을 ‘보존하기’를 바란다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 preserve(보존하다)가 알맞다. 미래엔(김성연) 2과

body:
We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to
Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but
wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he burst into a
song that he had taught Auntie. They sang
together, raising their voices to send the song flying like birds across the sky.
Just before noon, we arrived at a small town
called Murupara. “Where do we go now?” I asked
Nani. He did not reply, but he was searching inside
himself, ⓐstaring at the small houses. Then, at a
street corner, he told us to turn. After turning the
corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a
house. He welcomed Nani Tama with a ⓑgentle
smile, but in his eyes, I saw the message, “We must hurry.”
Now that day seems like a dream to me. I
remember the two old men sitting at the table and
the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked.
All through the quiet afternoon and into the
evening, they ⓒrecalled missing names. I had a
strange feeling that there were other people in the
room. I felt as if people from the past were looking
over the shoulders of the two old men to see if
the work was correct.
Finally, they stopped. It was done. After a
moment of silence, the old man ⓓwhispered to
Nani, “Goodbye, friend.” Crying, they pressed their
noses together to say goodbye.
It was early morning and still dark when we
returned to Auntie’s place. All the lights were on,
and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling,
Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it
to the village. Our hearts were full because our
grandfather had ⓔsaved our past for us.
Our Nani Tama smiled again. His smile grew tired.
He sighed. “At last, I may go now.” Then, he closed
his eyes. “No, Dad!” Auntie Hiraina cried. The sun
burst across the hills.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ stare: to look at something or someone for a long time without blinking or looking away
ⓑ gentle: kind, calm, and careful not to hurt or upset anyone or anything
ⓒ recall: to remember something from the past
ⓓ whisper: to speak very softly, using only a little breath, so that only a few people can hear
ⓔ save: to set aside money or resources for future use
solution:
① ⓐ~ⓓ의 풀이는 글에 쓰인 뜻(응시하다, 온화한, 기억해 내다, 속삭이다)과 맞는다.
② ⓔ saved our past for us는 할아버지가 잊힐 뻔한 족보(과거)를 '지켜 내다, 구해 내다(to keep something safe from being lost or destroyed)'라는 뜻이다.
③ ⑤의 풀이는 '(돈·자원을) 모아 두다, 저축하다'라는 다른 뜻이므로 알맞지 않다.
따라서 답은 ⑤이다.

solution: (A) 나니의 모습을 보고 그의 여행을 말리고 있으므로 나니의 건 강 상태가 매우 안 좋았음을 알 수 있다. 따라서 나니 타마가 얼 마나 thin(말랐는지)를 보고 충격 받았다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. (B) 와카파파를 다 마치지도 못한 상태에서 가만히 앉아서 죽 음을 기다리는 대신 고통스럽고 힘들더라고 와카파파를 마무 리하러 가겠다는 강한 의지를 소리치며 보여주고 있으므로, 화 자가 그를 말렸을 때 분노의 감정을 느꼈다는 흐름이 자연스 럽다. 따라서 anger(화)가 난 상태로 화자에게 말했다는 표현이 오는 것이 알맞다. (C) 그가 딸에게 가르쳐준 노래였다고 하고 둘이 같이 목소리를 높여 불렀다는 내용이 이어지므로 나니가 딸에게 가르쳐줬던 노 래를 burst into(갑자기 불렀다)라는 표현이 흐름상 자연스럽다.

For some time, ⓐmy grandfather had been busy
writing down the village genealogy, knowing as the
whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old
house. But then came the night of the fire, which
ran through the house and (A)[destroyed / glorified]
our past. In only one night, everything we knew
was gone. Nani Tama, in (B)[despair / hope], went
to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina.
Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past,
Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his
shaky hands. He chanted the names of the ancestors,
(C)[joining / attributing] the past to the present
once more. The village went quiet and listened to
his chanting. ⓑHis voice traveled along the lines of
our genealogy, searched back across the centuries.
Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to
remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the
middle of the chant. The village waited in worried
silence until the next name burst out of his mouth.
It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most
of the whakapapa, but there were still missing
names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to
drive him to Murupara to finish his work.

body:
Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing,
which has been a culturally significant practice of
the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only
decorative but also symbolic of an individual’s
journey from their past to their present. Each
curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a
person’s whakapapa(genealogy), social positions, and
personal accomplishments. This explains why no two
tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the
Maori have considered the head to be the most
sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their
faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire
faces, while women have it on their lips and chins.
The Maori start getting these designs in their
teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines
and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect
their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held
great importance as a rite of passage throughout
their lives. Although tā moko is less common these
days, it is still practiced today by Maori people,
who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage
for the next generation.

When I arrived at Auntie’s place, I was (A)[shocking
/ shocked] to see how thin Nani Tama was. “Look,
Nani,” I said. “I’m not taking you anywhere. You
could die on me!” Nani looked at me in anger.
“You want me to die here in this room? Looking at
these four walls? When the whakapapa is not yet
finished?” The old man held on tightly to the side
of the bed and cried out as he stood up. Every
slow, painful (B)[step / steps] hurt him, but he tried
to walk. I could not help but carry him to the car,
and we set off with Auntie. We traveled all night,
mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the
darkness. It was strange but wonderful to hear him.
Sometimes, he burst into a song (C)[that / what] he
had taught Auntie. They sang together, lifting up
their voices to send the song flying like a bird
through the sky.
(A)
(B)
(C)

me!” Nani looked at me in anger. “You want me to
die here in this room? Looking at these four walls?
When the whakapapa is (A)___________________?”
The old man held on tightly to the side of the
bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow,
painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could
not help but carry him to the car, and we set off
with Auntie.
We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to
Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but
wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he burst into a
song that he had taught Auntie. They sang
together, lifting up their voices to send the song
flying like a bird through the sky.

evening, they recalled missing names. I had a

of silence,

solution: (A) 완전한 절(we ~ town)에 이어져 앞의 명사구 a small town 을 수식하는 분사구로, 수식을 받는 명사구 a small town가 무 루파라라고 ‘불려지는’ 대상이므로, 수동의 의미를 지닌 과거분 사 called가 오는 것이 어법상 적절하다. Western countries, it’s okay to open gifts right
away, but in China, it’s considered rude. Similarly,
touching a person’s head, including that of a child,
is impolite in Thailand and Laos, whereas it may be
no big deal in other countries. So it’s important to

The phone rang, and it was my dad calling from
my hometown, Waituhi. “Can you take a week off?”
he asked. “Your Nani Tama wants you here.” “But
Dad!” I answered. “My boss won’t let me take any
more time off.” The phone went silent, and then I
heard my grandfather say faintly, “I need your help,
Grandson. I must go to Murupara to finish the
whakapapa. Drive me there. Hurry, I may not have
much time.” I just knew I had no choice. “All right,
Nani,” I replied with a sigh. “I’ll come.”

body:
For some time, my grandfather had been busy
writing down the village genealogy, known as the
whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old
house. But then came the night of the fire, which
ran through the house and destroyed our past. In
only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani
Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter,
my Auntie Hiraina.
Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past,
Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his
shaky hands. He chanted the names of the
ancestors, joining the past to the present once
more. The village went quiet and listened to his
chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our
genealogy, searching back across the centuries.
Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to
remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the
middle of the chant. The village waited in worried
silence until the next name burst out of his mouth.
It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most
of the whakapapa, but there were still missing
names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to
drive him to Murupara to finish his work.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: bringing peace to the family with chanting
overcoming Nani's despair through steady journaling
the challenges of rebuilding our lives after a big fire
restoring the whakapapa as a way to reconnectwith the past
Nani's hopelessness about failing to complete thewhakapapa
solution: 하룻밤의 화재로 인해 소실되어버린 와카파파를 복원하려는 나 니의 노력에 관한 내용이므로 글의 주제로 ❹ ‘과거와 다시 연결 되기 위한 방식으로서 와카파파를 복원하기‘가 가장 적절하다.

Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing,
which has been a culturally significant practice of the
Maori for thousands of years. It is not only
decorative but also symbolic of an individual’s
journey from their past to their present. (A) Each
curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a
person’s whakapapa(genealogy), social positions, and
personal accomplishments. (B) This explains why no
two tā moko designs look the same. (C) Traditionally,
the Maori have considered the head to be the most
sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their
faces. (D) The permanence of facial tattoos makes
them a lifelong commitment, often leading to regret
or unforeseen consequences. (E) Men typically wear
tā moko over their entire faces, while women have
it on their lips and chins. The Maori start getting
these designs in their teenage years, and as they
grow older, more lines and shapes are added to
their
tattoos
to
reflect
their
life
experiences.
Tattooing traditionally held great importance as a
rite of passage throughout their lives. Although tā
moko is less common these days, it is still practiced

body:
Tā moko is the traditional Maori art of tattooing,
which has been a culturally significant practice of
the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only
decorative but also symbolic of an individual’s
journey from their past to their present. Each
curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a
person’s whakapapa(genealogy), social positions, and
personal accomplishments. This explains why no two
tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the
Maori have considered the head to be the most
sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their
faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire
faces, while women have it on their lips and chins.
The Maori start getting these designs in their
teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines
and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect
their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held
great importance as a rite of passage throughout
their lives. Although tā moko is less common these
days, it is still practiced today by Maori people,
who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage
for the next generation.

corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a
house. He welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle
smile, but in his eyes, I saw the message, “We must
hurry.”
Now that day seems like a dream to me. I
remember the two old men sitting at the table and
the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked.
All through the quiet afternoon and into the
evening, they recalled missing names. I had a
strange feeling that there were other people in the

has its own unique traditions and customs, from

no big deal in other countries. So it’s important to

ancestors, joining the past to the present once
more. The village went quiet and listened to his
chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our
genealogy, searching back across the centuries.

remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the
middle of the chant. The village waited in worried
silence until the next name burst out of his mouth.

which has been a culturally significant practice of
the Maori for thousands of years. It is not only
decorative but also symbolic of an individual’s

curved line and pattern of tā moko represents a

tā moko designs look the same. Traditionally, the
Maori have considered the head to be the most
sacred part of the body, so they mainly tattoo their
faces. Men typically wear tā moko over their entire
faces, while women have it on their lips and chins.
The Maori start getting these designs in their
teenage years, and as they grow older, more lines
and shapes are added to their tattoos to reflect
their life experiences. Tattooing traditionally held
great importance as a rite of passage throughout
their lives. Although tā moko is less common these
days, it is still practiced today by Maori people,
who hope to preserve their traditions and heritage
for the next generation.

The Principle of Sound Waves and Interference
Sound is ⓐproduced through vibrations (A)[that /
what] occur from a sound source, when the strings
of a guitar (B)[is / are] played, for instance. The
vibrations of the sound source cause the air to
vibrate and the sound (C)[travelling / to travel] as
waves, similar to the ripples created in a lake when
you ⓑthrow a stone. When these sound waves
reach our ears, the brain interprets them as sound.
Just as different ripples in water might overlap if
you throw two stones, sound waves can also
interfere with each other when they ⓒmeet. There
are two types of interference: constructive and
destructive. Constructive interference occurs when
the ⓓpeaks of two waves overlap, resulting in a
bigger wave and a louder sound. Destructive
interference, on the other hand, occurs when a
peak of one wave overlaps with a valley of another
wave, so they ⓔstrengthen each other and produce
a quieter sound, or no sound at all.

Have you ever wondered what happens to sound
waves when they enter our ears? Let’s take a closer
look. The journey starts from the external part of
the outer ear, (A)[that / which] gathers the waves
and directs them into the ear. The collected waves
then travel through the ear canal and reach the
eardrum located in the middle ear. When the
eardrum vibrates, these vibrations (B)[transmit / are
transmitted] to three small bones in the middle ear.
These bones make the vibrations stronger and then
pass them to a snail-shaped structure in the inner
ear. Inside this fluid-filled structure are tiny hair
cells. When the vibrations make waves in the fluid,
the tiny hair cells move and generate electrical
signals that travel to the auditory nerve. This nerve
carries the information to the brain, where the
signals are interpreted, allowing us (C)[hear / to
hear] sound. Undoubtedly, it is a quite remarkable
journey!

Sound is produced through vibrations that occur
from a sound source, when the strings of a guitar
are played, for instance. The vibrations of the sound
source cause the air to vibrate and the sound to
travel as waves, similar to the ripples created in a
lake when you throw a stone. When these sound
waves reach our ears, the brain interprets them as
sound. Just as different ripples in water might
overlap if you throw two stones, sound waves can
also interfere with each other when they meet.
There are two types of interference: constructive
and destructive. Constructive interference occurs
when the peaks of two waves overlap, resulting in
a bigger wave and a louder sound. Destructive
interference, on the other hand, occurs when a
peak of one wave overlaps with a valley of another
wave, so they cancel each other out and produce a
quieter sound, or no sound at all.
Sound is produced through vibrations that create
waves, and as these waves travel, they can
(A)________________ each other in either a constructive
or destructive manner, (B)________________ the volume
of sound.
(A)                 (B)

Did you know that you can grow tasty mushrooms
right in your home using spent coffee grounds?
Coffee grounds contain the perfect nutrients for
growing mushrooms. (A)여기 당신이 버섯 키우기를
시작하는 데 도움을 주는 단계별 안내가 있다. First,
mix 80 percent coffee grounds with 20 percent
mushroom spawn. Then, thoroughly wash a milk
container and make four small holes in the sides.
Fill the container about two-thirds full of the mixture
and close it tightly. Next, find a warm and dark
place with a temperature between 18 and 25˚C, and
place the container there for two to four weeks
until the mixture turns completely white. When this
happens, move the container to a bright area with
indirect sunlight and cut the top off. To keep the
mixture from drying out, spray it with water twice a
day. Within a week, you will notice tiny mushrooms
emerging. When the mushrooms grow tall, they are
ready to be picked. After that, you can enjoy your
mushrooms with your favorite dish!

coffee grounds from its shops. These grounds are

(B)[resulted / resulting] SCGs are sold to fertilizer
companies, where they are transformed into organic
fertilizer. This fertilizer is later sold back to the
coffee shop chain. The chain provides the fertilizer
to local eco-friendly farmers, (C)[who / that] then
sell their produce back to the chain. The farm

such as rice chips and dried sweet potatoes, which
are sold in the chain’s coffee shops. By repurposing

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

So, what happens to all the waste from the coffee
extraction process? Spent coffee grounds (SCGs) are
classified as general waste and sent to landfills.
There they break down, releasing methane, a
greenhouse gas that is approximately 25 times
more potent than CO₂. Some SCGs are incinerated
instead of being buried, but this releases a lot of
CO₂: 338 kg per ton. However, neither of these
waste management options takes into account the
potential value of coffee grounds. Although the
grounds contain valuable organic compounds and
minerals, they are simply destroyed.
Fortunately, thanks to increased awareness of the
coffee waste problem, companies, organizations, and
governments around the world are working hard to
improve the environmental impact of the coffee
industry through circular economy measures. A
circular economy promotes the reuse of resources
for as long as possible, reducing waste and
environmental costs.

Did you know that you can grow tasty mushrooms
right in your home using spent coffee grounds?
Coffee grounds contain the perfect nutrients for
growing mushrooms. (A)여기 당신이 버섯 키우기를
시작하는 데 도움을 주는 단계별 안내가 있다. First,
mix 80 percent coffee grounds with 20 percent
mushroom spawn. Then, thoroughly wash a milk
container and make four small holes in the sides.
Fill the container about two-thirds full of the mixture
and close it tightly. Next, find a warm and dark
place with a temperature between 18 and 25˚C, and
place the container there for two to four weeks
until the mixture turns completely white. When this
happens, move the container to a bright area with
indirect sunlight and cut the top off. To keep the
mixture from drying out, spray it with water twice a
day. Within a week, you will notice tiny mushrooms
emerging. When the mushrooms grow tall, they are
ready to be picked. After that, you can enjoy your
mushrooms with your favorite dish!

An example of a circular economy in action occurs
when a chain of coffee shops collaborates with an
organization to collect spent coffee grounds from
its shops. These grounds are processed to remove
impurities and dried out. The resulting SCGs are
sold
to
fertilizer
companies,
where
they
are

Did you know that you can grow tasty mushrooms right in your home using spent coffee grounds? Coffee grounds contain the perfect nutrients for growing mushrooms. Here is a step-by-step guide to help you get started. First, mix 80 percent coffee grounds with 20 percent mushroom spawn. Then, thoroughly wash a milk container and make four small holes in the sides. Fill the container about two-thirds full of the mixture and close it tightly. Next, find a warm and dark place with a temperature between 18 and 25˚C, and place the container there for two to four weeks until the mixture turns completely white. When this happens, move the container to a bright area with indirect sunlight and cut the top off. To keep the mixture from drying out, spray it with water twice a day. Within a week, you will notice tiny mushrooms emerging. When the mushrooms grow tall, they are ready to be picked. After that, you can enjoy your mushrooms with your favorite dish! (1) Why are spent coffee grounds useful for growing mushrooms? → It’s because they ___________________________________ ___________________ for growing mushrooms. (2) What is necessary to prevent the mixture from drying out? → To prevent the mixture from drying out, it is necessary to ______________________________________.
answer: contain the perfect nutrients spray it with water twice a day

Let Bears Bear the Right to Live Freely
Bears are a ⓐfascinating group of animals with
eight species, all living in very different habitats
around the world. Polar bears, for example, live in
the Arctic, whereas Andean bears live in South
America. These bears should have the freedom ⓑto
live, but they are often killed when they come into
contact with humans. One of the worst ⓒexample
of this is bear bile farming. Brown bears in Eurasia
and North America, Sun bears in Southeast Asia,
and Asiatic black bears in Asia are often ⓓhunting
and keeping illegally for their bile, which is sold at
a high price for traditional Asian medicine. Although bile
farming is prohibited in many countries, it ⓔcontinues
due to the constant demand. (A)정부와 동물 복지
단체들은 이러한 농장들을 찾아 곰들을 구조하려는 지
속적인 시도들을 하며, 그들이 곰 보호 구역들이나 다
른 안전한 장소들에서 살 수 있게 한다. Since
UNESCO stated in 1978 ⓕthat animals are born
with the right to be respected, progress has been
made in animal rights. However, some animals are
still not fully protected outside the law, and ⓖneeds
more of our attention and care.

(B)

solution: (A) 앞의 명사구 a special place를 선행사로 하고 주어와 자동 사(live), 부사구로 이루어진 완전한 절(rescued ~ environment) 을 이끌고 있으므로 장소의 관계부사 where가 알맞다. (B) 동사 agreed의 목적어 자리에서 완전한 절(the ~ care)을 이끌고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다. 참고로, 관계대 명사·의문대명사 what은 주어, 목적어, 또는 보어가 없는 불완 전한 절을 이끌어 명사절을 이룬다. (C) Being이 생략된 분사구문에서 생략된 Being의 보어 역할을 하는 형용사 자리이며, 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 we가 ‘들뜨게 된’ 대상 이므로 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사형 형용사 Excited가 알맞다.

Let Bears Bear the Right to Live Freely
Bears are a fascinating group of animals with eight
species, all living in very different habitats around
the world. Polar bears, for example, (A)[live / living]
in the Arctic, whereas Andean bears live in South
America. These bears should have the freedom to
live, but they are often killed when they come into
contact with humans. One of the worst examples of
this is bear bile farming. Brown bears in Eurasia and
North America, Sun bears in Southeast Asia, and
Asiatic black bears in Asia are often hunted and kept
illegally for their bile, which (B)[is / are] sold at a
high price for traditional Asian medicine. Although
bile farming is prohibited in many countries, it
continues due to the constant demand. Governments
and animal welfare organizations make persistent
attempts to find these farms and rescue the bears,
allowing them (C)[live / to live] in bear sanctuaries or
other safe places. Since UNESCO stated in 1978 that
animals are born with the right to be respected,
progress has been made in animal rights. However,
some animals are still not fully protected outside the
law, and need more of our attention and care.
(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 주절의 주어 Polar bears와 두 개의 콤마(,) 사이에 삽입된 접속부 사 for example에 이어지는 문장의 동사 자리이므로 live가 알맞다. (B) 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 이끄는 절의 동사 자리에서 수동태(be동사+p.p.)를 이루는 be동사 자리로, 관계 사절이 부연 설명하고 있는 선행사 their bile이 단수명사구이 므로, 단수동사로 수일치한 is가 알맞다. 참고로, ‘쓸개즙, 담즙’ 을 뜻하는 bile은 불가산명사이므로 단수로 쓰였다. (C) 현재분사 형태로 쓰인 allowing과 목적어인 them에 이어지는 목적격보어 자리이며, ‘allow+목적어+목적격보어’의 5형식 구문에 서 allow는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하므로 to live가 알맞다. 미래엔(김성연) 1과

G: Hello, everyone! I’m Kelly. Are you thinking of
adopting a hamster? Today, I’d like to share
what I’ve learned from raising my hamster. First
of all, it’s important to understand that hamsters
are quite sensitive. While many people think that
taking care of hamsters is easy, they actually
require a lot of special attention. For example,
hamsters are active at night and sleep during
the day, so it’s crucial to provide a quiet
environment during the day. Also, their living
areas need to be cleaned regularly, and they
should be provided with fresh food and water
every day. One final tip: hamsters have poor
vision but have a strong sense of hearing. So,
try to spend some time talking to them near
their cage, and you’ll be amazed at how they
recognize your voice and respond to it. Keep
these tips in mind and take responsibility for
your hamster’s care.

Our club arrived at the Free Animals sanctuary.

Bears are a fascinating group of animals with eight
species, all living in very different habitats around
the world. Polar bears, for example, live in the
Arctic, whereas Andean bears live in South America.
These bears should have the freedom to live, but
they are often killed when they come into contact
with humans. One of the worst examples of this is
bear bile farming. Brown bears in Eurasia and North
America, Sun bears in Southeast Asia, and Asiatic
black bears in Asia are often hunted and kept
illegally for their bile, which is sold at a high price
for traditional Asian medicine. Although bile farming
is prohibited in many countries, it continues due to
the constant demand. Governments and animal
welfare organizations make persistent attempts to
find these farms and rescue the bears, allowing
them to live in bear sanctuaries or other safe
places. Since UNESCO stated in 1978 that animals
are born with the right to be respected, progress
has been made in animal rights. However, some
animals are still not fully protected outside the law,
and need more of our attention and care.

Why are bears illegally captured and raised onbear bile farms?
Even though bile farming is banned in manycountries, why does it still continue?
How many countries still allow legal bear bilefarming today?
What do governments and animal welfare organizationskeep doing for bears?

Let Bears Bear the Right to Live Freely
Bears are a fascinating group of animals with eight
species, all living in very different habitats around
the world. Polar bears, for example, live in the
Arctic, whereas Andean bears live in South America.
These bears should have the freedom to live, but
they are often killed when they come into contact
with humans. One of the worst examples of this is
bear bile farming. Brown bears in Eurasia and North
America, Sun bears in Southeast Asia, and Asiatic
black bears in Asia are often hunted and kept
illegally for their bile, which is sold at a high price
for traditional Asian medicine. Although bile farming
is prohibited in many countries, it continues due to
the constant demand. Governments and animal
welfare organizations make persistent attempts to
find these farms and rescue the bears, allowing
them to live in bear sanctuaries or other safe
places. Since UNESCO stated in 1978 that animals
are born with the right to be respected, progress
has been made in animal rights. However, __________
______________________________________________, and need
more of our attention and care.
choices: most animal rights issues have been solved by newlaws
some animals are still not fully protected outsidethe law
uses of animals for profit are a natural part ofhuman survival
public interests in animal welfare have made illegalanimal trade nearly disappear
endangered species around the world are nowcarefully managed through global cooperation
solution: 정부와 동물 복지 단체가 곰을 구조하려는 시도를 지속적으로 하고 있고 유네스코가 1978년에 동물도 존중받을 권리를 가지 고 태어난다고 공표한 이후 동물권에 대한 진전이 이루어졌다 는 긍정적인 변화를 언급한 뒤 However(하지만)로 이어지며, 우리의 더 많은 관심과 보살핌이 필요하다는 내용이 뒤에 언 급되므로, 여전히 동물권과 관련한 문제가 지속되고 있다는 흐 름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❷ ‘몇몇 동물들은 여전히 법의 테두리 밖에서 완전히 보호받지 못하고 있다’가 알맞다.

farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man
after the American Civil War, he still had to face
(B)[racial / religious] discrimination, working for very
low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around
70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of
Montgomery, Alabama, ⓒwhere he found a job in
a factory. ⓓIt wasn’t until he was 85 years old and
became too ill to work that he turned to drawing
to express his life experiences. Now, we’re going to
look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean
Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong
fear of dogs because they had often been used on
farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is
expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast,
Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays
the free lives of African Americans that he observed
on the streets of Montgomery. ⓔUsing simple shapes
and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in

two roles may appear similar, they actually have
quite different responsibilities, requiring different
skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin
word meaning “to teach,” docents are guides who
lead museum tours and provide information about
the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition.
They are usually volunteers who have a passion for
art and enjoy (A)[sharing / questioning] their
knowledge.
To
carry
out
their
responsibilities
effectively, docents need specialized training in
presentation and communication skills. On the other
hand, curators are professionals who design and
organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming
from a Latin word meaning “to take care of.”
Curators
determine
the
main
theme
of
each
exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme,
and arrange them in an engaging way which
(B)[captivates / distracts] the audience. Curators are
typically employed by museums and are expected
to possess advanced degrees in art history, museum
studies, or a related field. Despite their (C)[distinct /
similar] roles, both docents and curators share a
common goal: enriching every visitor’s experience.

exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from
Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may
notice a common theme — they all feature female
figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later
moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting
school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris,
(A)[which / in which] was unusual for women at the
time. Thanks to her mother’s encouragement, she
was able to take advantage of these opportunities.
Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in
painting, (B)[objecting / objected] to the social
pressure that married women were to solely focus
on household duties. Ancher differed from other

If you have ever been to an art museum, you may
have encountered docents and curators. While these
two roles may appear similar, they actually have
quite different responsibilities, requiring different
skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin
word meaning “to teach,” docents are guides who
lead museum tours and provide information about
the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition.
They are usually volunteers who have a passion for
art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out
their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized
training in presentation and communication skills.
On the other hand, curators are professionals who
design and organize exhibitions, with the word
curator coming from a Latin word meaning “to take
care of.” Curators determine the main theme of
each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the
theme, and arrange them in an engaging way
which captivates the audience. Curators are typically
employed by museums and are expected to possess
advanced degrees in art history, museum studies, or
a related field. Despite _______________________________,
both docents and curators share a common goal:
enriching every visitor’s experience.

choices: Docent vs. Curator: Who Controls the Art?
Docents and Curators Competing for PersonalFame
Docent and Curator, the Future of Artistic Professions
Docent vs. Curator: Experts Enhancing OurExperiences of Art
From Docents to Curators: Tracing the Evolutionof Museum Professions

Maud Lewis
Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist
ⓐknown for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a
small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from
physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and
fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to
drop out of school. To make a living, she began to
paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents
passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in
Digby, Nova Scotia, ⓑwhich she met her future
husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple
spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis
continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby
landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby
Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and
vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an
original, innovative style. ⓒAlthough her physical
limitations confined her to a small cottage, her
talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red
Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter
landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows
ⓓstanding in a flower field. With these features,
Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of
a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained
popularity, her story inspired many people and
ⓔlater made into books and movies. Maud Lewis
expressed her love for the world through her
paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian
folk art.

skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin

determine
the

of

Neuroscience has a long history of exploring
treatments for disorders of the nervous system,
including the brain and spinal cord. Traditionally,
researchers have studied various functions of neural
implants, which are medical devices like computer
chips that can be ⓐimplanted in the nervous
system. But here’s the exciting part: with the rapid
advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), researchers
have begun to ⓑintegrate AI into neural implants.
In this post, we’ll examine the incredible benefits of
AI-powered
neural
implants,
(A)their
amazing
potential for the future, and the ethical concerns
surrounding them.
First, let’s explore how this fascinating technology
has been applied. The AI-powered neural implant has
shown great promise in medical applications, offering
solutions to a range of problems. For instance,
neural implants are used to ⓒtreat brain disorders
like Parkinson’s disease. These implants electrically
ⓓstimulate targeted regions of the brain at the right
time with the help of AI to restore normal brain
activity. In addition, paralyzed people can have the
ability to walk again with the help of a “digital
bridge” between two implants inserted into their
brain and spine. When (B)they think about moving
their legs, the AI analyzes the brain signals and
sends (C)them to their legs through the implants.
Similarly, those who have lost their arms can use
artificial arms operated by the same ⓔmechanism.

Before we can fully embrace the era of AI-powered
neural implants, many tricky ethical issues should be
addressed. The integration of AI technology with the
human brain raises concerns about what it means to
be human. Our brains are believed to be central to
our identity, existence, and value as human beings.
However, ⓐan over-reliance on technology may delay
our natural development and (A)[create / resolve]
confusion about whether we are human, AI, or
something in between. Another critical issue is privacy.
There’s a risk that organizations or hackers could
access personal data without permission through
AI-connected implants. This means that our thoughts,
emotions, and behaviors could be controlled by
hackers. There’s an additional risk that this technology
could lead to even greater social inequality, given that
it may not be available to all due to its high cost.
Such (B)[equal / unequal] access to the technology
could intensify the division between those who can
afford the implants and those who cannot.
I hope that we can overcome these challenges
through careful consideration of neuroethics. This
field (C)[highlights / overlooks] the social aspects of
neural technology and provides possible answers to
what should be considered legal and ethical. I think
it is important to establish a prior review process
and thoroughly assess the ethical aspects before
any kind of brain research is conducted. This will
ensure that science and technology progress in
accordance with ethical principles.
What do you think about this technology? Please
share your opinion in the comments section below.

might cause. I think it is necessary to strictly
enforce privacy laws to protect the personal
information of individuals.

I’ll talk more about how to address the
concerns in my next post.

legs, have a rich history dating back to ancient times.

toe on an Egyptian mummy from around 950 B.C. In
the 16th century, a German knight known as Götz of

spring-operated fingers so that he could hold his
weapon more tightly. During the World Wars of the

Bill Traylor was born into slavery in 1853 on an Alabama plantation, and even after he became a freeman, he remained on the same land working as a farm laborer to support his large family. After spending decades in rural areas, he moved to the city of Montgomery around 1928, where he began a remarkable second life as an artist in his eighties. Living on the streets, Traylor drew on discarded cardboard to depict his memories of the past and the changing African American culture, creating a unique visual language despite being illiterate. His work was recognized and saved by local artist Charles Shannon, and although Traylor died in 1949, a major exhibition in 1982 finally brought his artistic genius to the world's attention.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I'm Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you're going to meet three amazing artists who never gave up on their art, despite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly valued. Let's explore each artist's life and artwork. The first artist we're going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a factory. It wasn't until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we're going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he's now considered an important figure in American folk art.
choices: Bill Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853.
Bill Traylor moved to Montgomery when he was around 70 years old.
Bill Traylor started drawing when he was 85 years old and too ill to work.
Bill Traylor feared dogs because they were used to watch and hunt slaves.
Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella shows Bill Traylor's fear of dogs.
solution: ⑤가 지문에서 Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella는 Traylor가 Montgomery 거리에서 관찰한 아프리카계 미국인들의 자유로운 삶을 묘사한다고 했으므로, 개에 대한 두려움을 나타낸다는 선택지는 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. ① Bill Traylor가 1853년 미국에서 노예로 태어났다는 내용은 지문과 일치한다. ② Bill Traylor가 70세 무렵 Montgomery로 이사했다는 내용은 지문과 일치한다. ③ Bill Traylor가 85세에 너무 아파 일을 할 수 없게 되었을 때 그림을 시작했다는 내용은 지문과 일치한다. ④ Bill Traylor가 개를 두려워했던 이유가 개들이 노예를 감시하고 사냥하는 데 사용되었기 때문이라는 내용은 지문과 일치한다.

Now let's take a look at the final artist of this exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may notice a common theme—they all feature female figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris, which was unusual for women at the time. Thanks to her mother's encouragement, she was able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting, objecting to the social pressure that married women were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher differed from other artists of that era, who depicted women as still life subjects. In contrast, she showcased them as active participants in everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman's Wife. 그녀는 또한 빛과 색을 능숙하게 탐구하면서, 덴마크의 풍성한 인 상주의 운동에 기여했다. In her painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us to this day.
Thank you for joining this guided tour, and I hope my explanations have aided you in appreciating these paintings. Please take some time to further explore the exhibition.

다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I'm Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you're going to meet three amazing artists who never gave up on their art, despite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly valued. Let's explore each artist's life and artwork. The first artist we're going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a factory. It wasn't until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we're going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he's now considered an important figure in American folk art.
choices: to introduce Bill Traylor's life and paintings to gallery visitors
to explain the history of slavery in Alabama
to advertise the Dream Art Gallery's upcoming events
to compare different styles of American folk art
to describe how Bill Traylor learned to draw at a factory 실전 모의고사 1회차

To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.
choices: renowned : widely known and admired by many people
distorted : perfectly straight and beautifully shaped
mobility : the ability to remember things clearly
innovative : following only old and traditional methods
confined : encouraged to travel freely everywhere
solution: ①의 renowned 는 “유명한, 널리 알려진”이라는 뜻으로, “widely known and admired by many people”는 올바른 영영 풀이이다. 반면 나머지는 모두 어휘 뜻과 맞지 않는다. distorted : 일그러진, 변형된 mobility : 움직일 수 있는 능력 innovative : 혁신적인 confined : 제한된, 갇힌 미래엔(김) 3과 실전 모의고사 1회차

다음 중 영영풀이와 단어가 잘못 연결된 것은?
Now let's take a look at the final artist of this exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may notice a common theme—they all feature female figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris, which was unusual for women at the time. Thanks to her mother's encouragement, she was able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting, objecting to the social pressure that married women were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher differed from other artists of that era, who depicted women as still life subjects. In contrast, she showcased them as active participants in everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman's Wife. She also skillfully explored light and color, contributing to the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us to this day. Thank you for joining this guided tour, and I hope my explanations have aided you in appreciating these paintings. Please take some time to further explore the exhibition.
ⓐfeature: to not include something or someone
ⓑencourage: to give someone support or confidence to do something
ⓒpersist: to keep doing something even when it is difficult
ⓓdiffer: to be unlike someone or something else
ⓔamaze: to make someone feel very surprised and impressed
solution: ① 제시된 풀이 'to not include something or someone(무언가나 누군가를 포함하지 않다)'은 feature(특징으로 포함하다)의 뜻과 반대이다. feature의 올바른 풀이는 'to include someone or something as an important part(중요한 부분으로 포함하다)'이다. ② encourage(격려하다): 무언가를 할 수 있도록 지지나 자신감을 주다 ③ persist(지속하다): 어렵더라도 계속해서 무언가를 하다 ④ differ(다르다): 다른 사람이나 사물과 같지 않다 ⑤ amaze(놀라게 하다): 누군가를 매우 놀랍고 인상적으로 느끼게 만들다

body:
밑줄 친 단어의 영영 풀이로 틀린 것은?
From Shadows to Spotlights Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I’m Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you’re going to meet three amazing artists who never gave up on their art, despite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly valued. Let’s explore each artist’s life and artwork. The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he’s now considered an important figure in American folk art.
choices: docent : a person who guides visitors in a museum or art gallery
slavery : the condition of being owned and forced to work by another person
discrimination : fair treatment of people regardless of their background
wage : money paid to workers for their labor or services
portray : to show or describe someone or something in a work of art or writing
solution: 본문에서 discrimination은 he still had to face racial discrimination과 같이 사용되어 인종 때문에 부당한 대우를 받는 것을 의미한다. 따라서 discrimination은 “차별”이라는 뜻이어야 한다. 하지만 ③의 영영 풀이인 fair treatment of people regardless of their background는 “배경과 관계없이 사람들을 공정하게 대우하는 것”이라는 의미이므로 원래 뜻과 반대되어 틀린 설명이다. 반면 나머지는 모두 올바른 영영 풀이이다. ① docent : 박물관이나 미술관에서 관람객을 안내하는 사람 → ‘전시 안내인’ ② slavery : 다른 사람에게 소유되어 강제로 일해야 하는 상태 → ‘노예 제도, 노예 상태’ ④ wage : 노동이나 서비스의 대가로 지급되는 돈 → ‘임금’ ⑤ portray : 예술 작품이나 글에서 사람이나 사물을 묘사하다 → ‘묘사하다’

다음 글을 통해 추론할 수 있는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
If you have ever been to an art museum, you may have encountered docents and curators. While these two roles may appear similar, they actually have quite different responsibilities, requiring different skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin word meaning "to teach," docents are guides who lead museum tours and provide information about the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition. They are usually volunteers who have a passion for art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized training in presentation and communication skills. On the other hand, curators are professionals who design and organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming from a Latin word meaning "to take care of." Curators determine the main theme of each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme, and arrange them in an engaging way which captivates the audience. Curators are typically employed by museums and are expected to possess advanced degrees in art history, museum studies, or a related field. Despite their distinct roles, both docents and curators share a common goal: enriching every visitor's experience.
choices: Docents are required to hold advanced degrees in art history before volunteering.
A docent's main focus is on selecting and arranging the artworks for an exhibition.
The word origins of docent and curator reflect the different focus of each role.
Curators mainly work as volunteers who assist docents during museum tours.
Both docents and curators receive the same type of specialized training. 유형보충독해1
solution: ③ docent는 '가르치다'라는 뜻의 라틴어에서, curator는 '돌보다'라는 뜻의 라틴어에서 유래했다고 했으므로, 각 단어의 어원이 두 역할의 서로 다른 초점, 즉 '가르침 vs 관리'를 반영한다는 것을 추론할 수 있다. ① 도슨트가 고급 학위를 요구받는다는 내용은 언급되지 않았으며, 고급 학위는 큐레이터에게 기대되는 자격이므로 적절하지 않다. ② 전시 작품을 선정하고 배치하는 것은 도슨트가 아니라 큐레이터의 역할이므로 적절하지 않다. ④ 큐레이터가 자원봉사자로 도슨트를 돕는다는 내용은 본문과 반대되며, 자원봉사자는 도슨트를 가리킨다. ⑤ 도슨트는 '발표, 의사소통 기술 훈련'을, 큐레이터는 '고급 학위'를 요구받으므로 동일한 훈련을 받는다는 내용은 적절하지 않다. 미래엔(김) 3과 실전 모의고사 1회차

Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis' paintings create a magical quality, like (A)that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.

다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Bill Traylor is a renowned folk artist who captured the key historical changes in American society. His works are especially valuable considering his passion for art despite many challenges in life. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination. Later, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama at the age of 70 to work at a factory. It wasn't until he was 85 years old that he quit working and turned to drawing to express his life experiences. In his paintings, Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog, Traylor reveals his strong fear of dogs, depicting them as a threatening beast. Because dogs had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves, his fear reflects his early life as a slave. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Through paintings, Traylor . As a result, he's now considered an important figure in American folk art.
choices: documented complicated moments in life where he submitted to his personal fear and weaknesses
fought back the racial discrimination towards the African American slaves in Montgomery
showcased his talent as a skilled farmer by expressing his life experience on a cotton farm
expressed the difficult journey of American history including slavery and the path to freedom

Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis' paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.

다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
If you have ever been to an art museum, you may have encountered docents and curators. While these two roles may appear similar, they actually have quite different responsibilities, requiring different skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin word meaning "to teach," docents are guides who lead museum tours and provide information about the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition. They are usually volunteers who have a passion for art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized training in presentation and communication skills. On the other hand, curators are professionals who design and organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming from a Latin word meaning "to take care of." solution: ⓐ '미술관에 가본 적이 있다면(have ever been)'이라는 과거의 경험을 바탕으로 한 추측을 나타내므로, 조동사 may 뒤에 완료형인 「have + 과거분사」를 써서 '~마주쳤을지도 모른다'라는 의미를 완성하는 것이 알맞다. ⓑ 「with + 명사 + 분사」 형태의 부대상황(동시동작) 구문이다. 도슨트라는 단어가 라틴어에서 '유래하는' 능동의 의미를 지니므로 현재분사(-ing) 형태가 알맞다. ⓒ 전시회에 '다뤄지는(포함되는)' 예술가들이라는 수동의 의미로 앞에 있는 명사(artists)를 뒤에서 수식해야 하므로 과거분사 형태가 알맞다. ⓓ 뒤에 오는 명사 교육(training)을 수식하며, '전문화된'이라는 수동 및 완료의 의미를 지니므로 과거분사 형태가 알맞다. ⓔ 큐레이터들이 고학력을 '소지할 것으로(to possess) 기대된다(are expected)'는 문맥이다. 주어가 수동의 입장이므로 수동태(be expected)를 쓰고, 그 뒤에 to부정사를 연결한 형태가 알맞다. 등위접속사 and에 의해 앞의 동사(are employed)와 병렬 구조를 이루므로 be동사는 are가 된다.

Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I’m Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you’re going to meet three amazing artists who never gave up on their art, despite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly valued. Let’s explore each artist’s life and artwork. The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he’s now considered an important figure in American folk art.

Ways to find a factory job in cities
The popularity of modern art in Europe
Bill Traylor's life and art from slavery to freedom

Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.

Now let’s take a look at the final artist of this exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may notice a common theme—they all feature female figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris, which was unusual for women at the time. Thanks to her mother’s encouragement, she was able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting, objecting to the social pressure that married women were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher differed from other artists of that era, who depicted women as still life subjects. In contrast, she showcased them active participants in everyday tasks, seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman’s Wife. She also skillfully explored light and color, contributing to the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us to this day.

solution: ④ Traylor는 개들이 농장에서 노예를 감시하고 사냥하는 데 자주 이용되었기 때문에 개를 몹시 두려워했다고 했으므로 일치한다. ① Isabel Williams는 전시회의 도슨트로 소개되었을 뿐 작품을 그렸다는 내용은 없으므로 일치하지 않는다. ② Traylor가 Montgomery로 이주한 것은 약 70세 때였으므로 일치하지 않는다. ③ Traylor는 85세에 몸이 너무 아파 일할 수 없게 되어서야 그림을 시작했으므로 정반대이다. ⑤ Man with Umbrella는 Traylor가 Montgomery 거리에서 실제로 관찰한 아프리카계 미국인들의 자유로운 삶을 그린 것이지 바라던 자유를 그린 것이 아니므로 일치하지 않는다.

(B) In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. solution: 주어진 글에서 Bill Traylor가 노예로 태어나 앨라배마의 목화 농장에서 일했다는 생애 초기의 배경을 소개한다. (C) 주어진 문장 뒤에는 시간의 흐름에 따라 남북전쟁 이후 자유인이 되었으나 70세까지 고된 삶을 살았고, 85세가 되어서야 비로소 삶의 경험을 표현하기 위해 '그림 그리기 (drawing)에 눈을 돌렸다'는 내용이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다. (A) (C)의 마지막 부분에서 그가 그림을 그리기 시작했다는 내용(turned to drawing)을 바탕으로, "Now, ~ (이제, 그의 그림들 중 일부를 살펴보자)"라며 구체적인 초기 작품들(개에 대한 두려움을 표현한 그림들)을 소개하는 (A)가 이어져야 한다. (B) 마지막으로, 연결어 "In contrast(대조적으로)"를 사용하여 (A)의 두려움을 표현한 그림들과 대비되는 '자유로운 삶'을 묘사한 작품(Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella)을 소개하고, 그의 예술적 의의를 평가하며 글을 마무리하는 (B)가 오는 것이 논리적이다. 따라서 가장 적절한 글의 순서는 ④가 가장 알맞다.

The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. solution: ⓐ valuing → valued 5형식 동사 made의 목적격보어 자리로, 목적어인 'their work'가 높이 평가 '받는' 수동의 관계이다. 따라서 현재분사 valuing을 과거분사 valued로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ to work → working 'spend + 시간 + -ing'는 '~하면서 시간을 보내다'라는 의미의 구문으로, spend 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 한다. 따라서 to부정사 to work를 동명사 working으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓓ used → been used 주어 they가 가리키는 dogs는 노예를 감시하고 사냥하는 데 '이용된' 대상이므로 수동태가 되어야 한다. 과거완료 수동태인 'had been p.p.'의 형태가 되도록 used를 been used로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ 외의 밑줄은 다음과 같은 이유로 옳다. ⓒ 'It wasn't until ~ that ...'은 '~하고 나서야 비로소 … 했다'라는 의미의 강조 구문이므로 that이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 Traylor가 단순한 형태와 색을 직접 사용하는 능동의 관계이므로 현재분사 Using이 올바르게 쓰였다.

Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I’m Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you’re going to meet three amazing artists who never gave up on their art, despite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly valued. Let’s explore each artist’s life and artwork. The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he’s now considered an important figure in American folk art.
choices: The featured artists in the exhibit continued their art in spite of personal difficulties.
Bill Traylor's freedom after the Civil War did not end the unfair treatment toward him.
Bill Traylor began his artistic career after leaving factory work due to poor health.
Bill Traylor's fear of dogs originated from a dog attack he suffered as a child.
Bill Traylor's artwork shows that simple techniques can convey deep historical meaning.
solution: ④ Traylor가 개를 두려워한 이유는 농장에서 개가 노예를 감시하고 쫓는 데 자주 쓰였기 때문이라고 했을 뿐, 어린 시절 개에게 공격당한 경험은 지문에 언급되지 않으므로 추론할 수 없다. ① 전시에 소개되는 세 예술가가 삶의 어려움에도 예술을 포기하지 않았다고 했으므로 개인적 역경 속에서도 작품 활동을 이어갔다고 추론할 수 있다. ② 남북전쟁 후 자유인이 되었지만 여전히 인종 차별과 저임금을 겪었다고 했으므로 자유를 얻은 뒤에도 부당한 대우가 이어졌다고 추론할 수 있다. ③ 몽고메리의 공장에서 일하다가 85세에 병으로 일할 수 없게 되고 나서야 그림을 시작했다고 했으므로 건강 악화로 공장 일을 그만둔 뒤 예술 활동을 시작했다고 추론할 수 있다. ⑤ 단순한 형태와 색채로 노예제에서 자유에 이르는 미국 역사의 복잡한 순간을 담아냈다고 했으므로 단순한 기법으로도 깊은 역사적 의미를 전달할 수 있다고 추론할 수 있다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
Now let’s take a look at the final artist of this exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may notice a common theme—they all feature female figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris, which was unusual for women at the time. Thanks to her mother’s encouragement, she was able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting, objecting to the social pressure that married women were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher differed from other artists of that era, who depicted women as still life subjects. In contrast, she showcased them as active participants in everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman’s Wife. She also skillfully explored light and color, contributing to the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us to this day. Thank you for joining this guided tour, and I hope my explanations have aided you in appreciating these paintings. Please take some time to further explore the exhibition.
choices: Anna Ancher was born in Skagen and later attended a painting school in Copenhagen.
Anna Ancher's father encouraged her to study at schools in Copenhagen and Paris.
Anna Ancher continued painting after marriage despite social pressure on married women.
Anna Ancher portrayed women as active people doing daily work, not still objects.
In Sunlight in the Blue Room, sunlight reflects off a blue wall.
solution: ② Ancher가 코펜하겐과 파리에서 공부할 기회를 활용할 수 있었던 것은 어머니의 격려 덕분이었다고 했으므로, 아버지가 격려했다는 선택지는 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. ① Skagen에서 태어나 이후 코펜하겐으로 이주해 사립 미술 학교에 다녔다는 내용과 일치한다. ③ 결혼 후에도 기혼 여성은 집안일에 집중해야 한다는 사회적 압력에 반대하며 그림을 계속 그렸다는 내용과 일치한다. ④ 여성을 정물처럼 그린 당대 화가들과 달리 여성을 일상 업무에 적극 참여하는 모습으로 표현했다는 내용과 일치한다. ⑤ 'Sunlight in the Blue Room'에서 파란 벽에 비친 햇빛의 반사가 멋지게 묘사되었다는 내용과 일치한다.

body:
다음 글의 내용으로 추론할 수 있는 것은?
Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.
choices: Maud Lewis earned money from her art before moving to Digby.
Maud Lewis met Everett Lewis while living with her parents in Nova Scotia.
Maud Lewis learned her painting style from folk artists living in Digby.
Maud Lewis's small living space restricted the range of subjects in her paintings.
Maud Lewis's work quickly won wide public recognition during her career.
solution: ① Lewis는 생계를 위해 크리스마스 카드를 그려 팔기 시작했고, 그 뒤 부모님이 돌아가시자 Digby로 옮겨 갔다고 했으므로, Digby로 이주하기 전부터 그림으로 돈을 벌었다고 추론할 수 있다. 따라서 ①이 정답이다. ② 부모님이 돌아가신 후 이모와 함께 살기 위해 Digby로 가서 미래의 남편을 만났다고 했으므로, 부모님과 함께 살던 중 남편을 만났다고 추론할 수 없다. ③ Lewis의 화풍이 독창적이고 혁신적이었다고만 했을 뿐 Digby의 민속 화가들에게서 배웠다는 내용은 없으므로 추론할 수 없다. ④ 신체적 제약으로 작은 오두막에 갇혀 지냈지만 재능과 상상력은 한계가 없었다고 했으므로, 좁은 생활 공간이 그림의 소재를 제한했다고 추론할 수 없다. ⑤ 그림이 점차 인기를 얻었다고 했으므로, 빠르게 대중의 폭넓은 인정을 받았다고 추론할 수 없다.
