밑줄 친 우리말과 일치하도록 <보기>의 단어들을 바르게 배열하시오.
Now let’s take a look at the final artist of this exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may notice a common theme—they all feature female figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris, which was unusual for women at the time. 어머니의 격려 덕분에, 그녀는 이러한 기회들을 활용할 수 있었다. Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting, objecting to the social pressure that married women were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher differed from other artists of that era, who depicted women as still life subjects. In contrast, she showcased them as active participants in everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman’s Wife. She also skillfully explored light and color, contributing to the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us to this day.
Thank you for joining this guided tour, and I hope my explanations have aided you in appreciating these paintings. Please take some time to further explore the exhibition.
보기 able / opportunities / her / take / Thanks / these / was / mother’s / of / she / to / advantage / encouragement / to
→
answer: Thanks to her mother’s encouragement, she was able to take advantage of these opportunities.
solution: ~ 덕분에'라는 의미의 'Thanks to'를 문장 맨 앞에 두고, 그 뒤에 명사구 'her mother’s encouragement'를 이어 쓴다. 주절은 주어 'she' 뒤에 '~할 수 있었다'라는 의미의 'was able to'를 쓰고, to 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 '~을 활용하다'라는 의미의 숙어 'take advantage of'를 연결한다. 마지막으로 'of'의 목적어로 'these opportunities'를 배치하여 문장을 완성한다.

body:
다음 글을 바탕으로 추론할 수 없는 것은?
The first artist we're going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a factory. It wasn't until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we're going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he's now considered an important figure in American folk art.
choices: The American Civil War brought a complete end to racial discrimination against African Americans.
Traylor's personal experiences heavily influenced the subjects of his drawings.
Some African Americans in Montgomery lived freely compared to the times of slavery.
Traylor did not make a living as a professional artist during his youth.
Physical illness became a turning point that led Traylor to start his artistic journey.
solution: ① 남북전쟁 이후 자유인이 되었음에도 여전히 인종 차별에 직면했다고 언급되어 있으므로, 남북전쟁이 인종 차별의 완전한 종식을 가져왔다는 내용은 추론할 수 없다. ② 자신이 두려워했던 개, 관찰했던 사람들을 그렸으므로 개인적 경험이 작품 주제에 영향을 미쳤음을 추론할 수 있다. ③ 몽고메리 거리에서 관찰한 흑인들의 자유로운 삶을 묘사했다는 부분에서 추론할 수 있다. ④ 젊은 시절 농장과 공장에서 일했고 85세에 그림을 시작했으므로 추론할 수 있다. ⑤ 너무 병들어 일할 수 없게 된 것이 그림을 그리게 된 계기가 되었으므로 추론할 수 있다. 미래엔(김) 3과 실전 모의고사 3회차

solution: ③ 주어 Ancher가 '결혼한 여성은 집안일에만 집중해야 한다는 사회적 압력'에 직접 반대하는 능동의 관계이므로, 현재분사로 시작하는 분사구문 objecting이 올바르게 쓰였다. ① observed → observing 'When ~ her paintings'는 주절의 주어 you가 그림을 관찰하는 능동의 의미를 나타내는 분사구문이다. 뒤에 목적어 'her paintings'가 있으므로 과거분사 observed를 현재분사 observing으로 고쳐야 한다. ② that → which 콤마 뒤에서 앞 절 'she even studied abroad in Paris' 전체를 선행사로 받는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사가 필요하다. 관계대명사 that은 계속적 용법으로 쓸 수 없으므로 which로 고쳐야 한다. ④ displaying → displayed 등위접속사 and는 주어 Ancher의 동사 challenged와 문법적으로 대등한 요소를 연결해야 한다. 따라서 현재분사 displaying을 과거시제 동사 displayed로 고쳐 병렬 구조를 맞춰야 한다. ⑤ appreciate → appreciating 'aid A in -ing' 구문에서 전치사 in의 목적어 자리이므로 동사원형 appreciate가 아니라 동명사 appreciating으로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art. 실전 모의고사 3회차
choices: Maud Lewis's physical condition allowed her to move around freely.
After her parents died, Maud Lewis moved in with her grandmother in Digby.
Maud Lewis learned oil painting techniques from her husband Everett Lewis.
Maud Lewis's talent was limited because she stayed in a small cottage.
Maud Lewis's life story was later turned into books and films.
solution: ⑤ 그림이 점차 인기를 얻으면서 그녀의 이야기가 많은 사람에게 영감을 주었고 이후 책과 영화로 만들어졌다고 했으므로, 지문의 내용과 일치한다. ① 신체적 약점이 그녀의 거동을 제한했다고 했으므로, 자유롭게 움직일 수 있었다는 진술은 지문의 내용과 정반대이다. ② 부모님이 돌아가신 후 Digby에 사는 이모(고모)와 함께 살러 갔다고 했으므로, 할머니와 살았다는 진술은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. ③ 남편 Everett Lewis에게서 유화 기법을 배웠다는 내용은 지문에 언급되지 않았으므로, 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. ④ 신체적 한계로 작은 오두막에 갇혀 지냈지만 재능과 상상력은 무한했다고 했으므로, 재능이 제한되었다는 진술은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않는다.

solution: ⓑ which → where 뒤에 이어지는 절 'she met her future husband, Everett Lewis'는 주어와 목적어를 모두 갖춘 완전한 절이다. 따라서 장소를 나타내는 선행사 'Digby, Nova Scotia'를 받으려면 관계대명사 which가 아니라 관계부사 where를 써야 한다. ⓒ generated → generating 분사구문의 의미상 주어는 주절의 주어 'Her artwork'이다. 작품이 독창적이고 혁신적인 스타일을 직접 만들어 낸다는 능동의 의미이고, 뒤에 목적어 'an original, innovative style'도 있다. 따라서 과거분사 generated를 현재분사 generating으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ making → made 주어 'her story'는 책과 영화로 '만들어지는' 대상이므로 수동의 의미이다. 따라서 'was later making'을 수동태 'was later made'로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ 주절의 주어 Lewis가 '태어난' 것이므로 수동의 의미이다. 따라서 과거분사로 시작하는 분사구문 Born이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓓ 소들이 '장식된' 대상이므로 명사 cows를 앞에서 수식하는 과거분사 decorated가 올바르게 쓰였다.

If you have ever been to an art museum, you may have encountered docents and curators. While these two roles may appear similar, they actually have quite different responsibilities, ⓐdemanding different skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin word meaning "to teach," docents are guides who lead museum tours and provide information about the artworks and artists
ⓑfeatured in an exhibition. They are usually volunteers who have a passion for art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To ⓒcarry out their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized training in presentation and communication skills. On the other hand, curators are professionals who design and organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming from a Latin word meaning "to take care of." Curators determine the main theme of each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme, and arrange them in an engaging way which ⓓdraws the audience in. Despite their ⓔidentical roles, both docents and curators share a common goal:
enriching every visitor's experience.

다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
If you have ever been to an art museum, you may have encountered docents and curators. While these two roles may appear similar, they actually have quite different responsibilities, requiring different skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin word meaning "to teach," docents are guides who lead museum tours and provide information about the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition. They are usually volunteers who have a passion for art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized training in presentation and communication skills. On the other hand, curators are professionals who design and organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming from a Latin word meaning "to take care of." Curators determine the main theme of each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme, and arrange them in an engaging way which captivates the audience. Curators are typically employed by museums and are expected to possess advanced degrees in art history, museum studies, or a related field. Despite their distinct roles, both docents and curators share a common goal: enriching every visitor's experience.
choices: Docents and curators have different roles but share a common goal.
Docents need advanced degrees in art history to guide museum tours.
Curators must have strong communication skills to attract visitors.
Art museums rely only on volunteers to manage their exhibitions.
Visitors enjoy museums more when they study art history in advance. 유형보충독해

Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical ⓐweaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis ⓑcontinued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an ⓒoriginal, innovative style. Although her physical limitations ⓓexpanded her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a ⓔmagical quality, like that of a fairy tale.
solution: ⓓ expanded → confined 문맥상 그녀의 '신체적 한계(physical limitations)'는 긍정적인 확장이 아니라 부정적인 제한을 가져왔다. 문장 구조상 '그녀를 작은 오두막집에 국한시켰다, 가두었다'라는 의미가 되어야 뒤에 이어지는 '하지만(Although) 상상력은 무한했다' 라는 내용과 역접의 대조를 이룰 수 있다. 따라서 '확장시켰다'라는 뜻의 expanded는 문맥에 맞지 않으며, confined(제한했다, 가두었다)와 같은 단어로 고쳐야 올바르다. ⓐ weaknesses: 약점 ⓑ continued: 계속되었다 ⓒ original: 독창적인 ⓔ magical: 마법같은

조건 1. 수동태를 사용할 것
2. (American folk art, now, important figure, as a result, consider)를 모두 포함할 것

answer: As a result, he’s now considered an important figure in American folk art.
solution: 그 결과'라는 의미의 연결어 'as a result'를 문장 맨 앞에 쓰고 쉼표로 구분한 뒤, 주어 'he'를 쓴다. '~로 여겨지다'는 동사 'consider'의 수동태로 표현해야 하므로 수동태 조건에 따라 be동사 'is'와 과거분사 'considered'를 추가하여 'he's now considered'로 쓰며, '현재'를 뜻하는 부사 'now'는 be동사와 과거분사 사이에 둔다. 'consider A B' 구문이 수동태로 바뀌면서 목적격보어 'an important figure'가 'considered' 바로 뒤에 오므로, 박스의 'important figure' 앞에 관사 'an'을 추가한다. 마지막으로 '미국 민속 예술에서'는 전치사 'in'을 추가하여 'in American folk art'로 완성한다.

다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I'm Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you're going to meet three amazing artists who never gave up on their art, despite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly valued. Let's explore each artist's life and artwork. The first artist we're going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a factory. It wasn't until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we're going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he's now considered an important figure in American folk art.
choices: Bill Traylor: From Slavery to a Folk Art Icon
The History of Cotton Farms in Alabama
How Dogs Were Used on American Farms
Famous Art Galleries Around the World
Bill Traylor's Fear of Dogs in His Paintings
solution: ① 이 지문은 노예로 태어나 온갖 차별과 어려움을 극복하고 85세에 그림을 시작하여 미국 민속 예술의 중요한 인물로 인정받은 Bill Traylor의 삶과 예술을 소개하고 있으므로, 글의 제목으로 가장 적절하다. ② 앨라배마 목화 농장에 대한 내용은 Traylor의 초기 삶을 설명하기 위한 배경일 뿐, 글 전체 주제인 Traylor의 삶과 예술을 포괄하지 못한다. ③ 개가 농장에서 어떻게 사용되었는지는 Traylor의 개에 대한 두려움을 설명하기 위한 세부 사례일 뿐, 글의 제목은 아니다. ④ 세계 유명 미술관에 대한 내용은 글에서 전혀 언급되지 않았다. ⑤ 개에 대한 두려움은 Traylor의 일부 작품에 국한된 내용으로, 글 전체가 전달하고자 하는 Traylor의 삶과 예술 전반을 담지 못한다. 미래엔(김) 3과

Now let’s take a look at the final artist of this exhibition:
Anna Ancher, a famous painter from Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may notice a common theme—they all feature female figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later moved to Copenhagen to attend a private painting school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris, which was unusual for women at the time. Thanks to her mother’s encouragement, she was able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting, objecting to the social pressure that married women were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher differed from other artists of that era, who depicted women as still life subjects. In contrast, she showcased them as active participants in everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman’s Wife. She also skillfully explored light and color, contributing to the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly portrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us to this day. Thank you for joining this guided tour, and I hope my explanations have aided you in appreciating these paintings. Please take some time to further explore the exhibition.

Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. (A) To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. (B) When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. (C) After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. (D) She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. (E) Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an original, innovative style. Due to her physical limitations, _____ . In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis' paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.

she turned away from the world of art, finding comfort only in solitude

she faced restrictions in her painting, which made some artistic techniques difficult to perform

If you have ever been to an art museum, you may have encountered docents and curators. While these two roles may appear similar, they actually have quite different responsibilities, requiring different skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin word meaning "to teach," docents are guides who lead museum tours and provide information about the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition. They are usually volunteers who have a passion for art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized training in presentation and communication skills. On the other hand, curators are professionals who design and organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming from a Latin word meaning "to take care of." Curators determine the main theme of each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme, and arrange them in an engaging way which captivates the audience. Curators are typically employed by museums and are expected to possess advanced degrees in art history, museum studies, or a related field. Despite their distinct roles, both docents and curators share a common goal: enriching every visitor's experience. Docent vs. Curator

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
If you have ever been to an art museum, you may have encountered docents and curators. While these two roles may appear similar, they actually have quite different responsibilities, requiring different skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin word meaning "to teach," docents are guides who lead museum tours and provide information about the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition. They are usually volunteers who have a passion for art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized training in presentation and communication skills. On the other hand, curators are professionals who design and organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming from a Latin word meaning "to take care of." Curators determine the main theme of each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme, and arrange them in an engaging way which captivates the audience. Curators are typically employed by museums and are expected to possess advanced degrees in art history, museum studies, or a related field. Despite their distinct roles, both docents and curators share a common goal: enriching every visitor's experience.
choices: Docents and curators need similar skills for their different duties.
The term docent has Latin roots meaning "to take care of."
Docents receive specialized training from curators before leading tours.
Curators pick works of art that match an exhibition's central theme.
Docents and curators share the aim of attracting more visitors to museums. 유형보충독해
solution: ④ 큐레이터는 각 전시의 주제를 정하고 그 주제에 어울리는 작품을 선정한다고 했으므로 일치한다. ① 두 역할은 비슷해 보이지만 책임이 서로 다르고 서로 다른 기술을 요구한다고 했으므로, 비슷한 기술이 필요하다는 진술은 지문의 내용과 정반대이다. ② docent는 '가르치다'를 뜻하는 라틴어에서 왔고, '돌보다'를 뜻하는 라틴어에서 온 단어는 curator이므로 일치하지 않는다. ③ 도슨트에게 발표와 의사소통에 관한 전문 훈련이 필요하다고만 했을 뿐, 그 훈련을 큐레이터에게 받는다는 내용은 없으므로 일치하지 않는다. ⑤ 두 직업의 공통 목표는 방문객의 수를 늘리는 것이 아니라 방문객의 경험을 풍부하게 하는 것이라고 했으므로 일치하지 않는다.

solution: ④ 도슨트는 대개 미술에 열정을 지닌 자원봉사자로서 발표와 의사소통 기술에 관한 훈련이 필요하다고 한 반면, 큐레이터는 박물관에 고용된 전문가로서 미술사나 박물관학 등의 고급 학위를 갖출 것이 기대된다고 했으므로, 큐레이터 직책이 도슨트보다 더 높은 학문적 자격을 요구한다고 추론할 수 있다. ① 도슨트는 '가르치다'라는 뜻의 라틴어에서, 큐레이터는 '돌보다'라는 뜻의 라틴어에서 유래했다고 했으므로, 두 단어가 같은 라틴어에서 왔다고 추론할 수 없다. ② 도슨트에게 필요한 훈련은 발표와 의사소통 기술이라고 했을 뿐 작품 복원 기술에 관한 언급은 없으므로 추론할 수 없다. ③ 큐레이터라는 말이 '돌보다'라는 뜻에서 왔다는 어원 정보만으로는 부족하며, 실제 업무는 전시 주제를 정하고 작품을 선정·배치하는 것이라고 했으므로 작품의 물리적 보호가 주된 임무라고 추론할 수 없다. ⑤ 도슨트와 큐레이터는 역할은 다르지만 방문객의 경험을 풍부하게 한다는 공통 목표를 지닌다고 했으므로, 서로 상충하는 목표를 추구한다고 추론할 수 없다.

His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. ⓓUsed simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. body:

A kangaroo's tail, ⓐthat is made up of over twenty vertebrae, acts as a powerful muscle for balance and movement. The tail works almost like a fifth leg ⓑso that the kangaroo can hop, turn, and even fight without losing stability. When a kangaroo stands still, its tail ⓒsupports most of its body weight while the legs rest. During a fight, a kangaroo often begins ⓓkicking its opponent with both hind legs while balancing on its tail. Before hopping away, the kangaroo tucks its front legs close to its chest to protect ⓔthem from injury. *vertebrae: 척추뼈
solution: ①ⓐ이 정답이다. 'A kangaroo's tail, that is made up of over twenty vertebrae'에서 콤마 뒤의 계속적 용법 관계대명사로는 'that'을 쓸 수 없으므로 'which'로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ 'so that'은 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어져 목적이나 결과를 나타내는 접속사로 올바르다. ⓒ 주어 'its tail'이 단수이므로 단수동사 'supports'가 알맞다. ⓓ 'begin + -ing' 구조에서 'kicking'이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ 'them'은 앞의 복수명사 'front legs'를 가리키는 대명사로 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
A bat's brain processes returning echoes ⓐso that it can determine the exact distance and shape of nearby objects in total darkness. As soon as a bat begins flying, it starts ⓑemitting a rapid series of high-pitched clicks. Each click
ⓒtravels outward until it hits an object and bounces back to the bat's ears. These returning signals, ⓓthat are analyzed within milliseconds, allow the bat to build a detailed map of its surroundings. A bat also uses its wings to catch insects, tucking them close to its body to keep
ⓔthem from escaping. *echo: 반향(음)
solution: ④ⓓ가 정답이다. 'These returning signals, that are analyzed within milliseconds'에서 콤마 뒤의 계속적 용법 관계대명사로는 'that'을 쓸 수 없으므로 'which'로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ 'so that'은 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어져 목적이나 결과를 나타내는 접속사로 올바르다. ⓑ 'start + -ing' 구조에서 'emitting'이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ 'Each click'은 단수 주어이므로 단수동사 'travels'가 알맞다. ⓔ 'them'은 앞의 복수명사 'insects'를 가리키는 대명사로 적절하다. 미래엔(김) 3과 문법 정복 실전
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
The majority of the refrigerators we have at home or in restaurants (A)[is / are] actually prone to picking up strong odors from food. They absorb smells easily, and most compartments aren't very well sealed. Spraying air freshener isn't a true solution, (B)[although / despite] what many advertisements claim. It can affect both the taste of stored food and your health, and the smell returns immediately anyway. A clever way to solve the odor problem is to place a small bowl with baking soda and charcoal and (C)[places / place] it inside the fridge or near the vents. The odor fades slowly through absorption — much less quickly than it will through the food itself — and keeps a little more freshness in the air around your fridge.
solution: (A)의 주어는 'The majority of the refrigerators'이며, 'majority of + 복수명사'는 복수 취급하므로 'are'가 알맞다. (B)의 'what many advertisements claim'은 명사절이므로 전치사 'despite'가 알맞다. (C)는 'to place ~ and place ~'의 병렬 구조이므로 동사원형 'place'가 알맞다. 따라서 정답은 ①이다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음을 읽고, 어법상 틀린 부분을 한 군데 찾아 바르게 고치시오.
Urban noise pollution has had positive influences on the way people adapt to city life and stay alert. However, although constant noise seems to be a normal part of city living, it is actually reducing people's ability to focus. The more time people spend in noisy environments, the less concentration they have. Many researchers now believe that noise pollution can lead to a number of cognitive problems. In fact, a recent study showed that traffic noise raises cortisol levels, that explains why people who live in noisy areas experience significant levels of stress, fatigue, and other cognitive issues.
→
solution: 콤마 다음에 와서 앞 절 전체를 선행사로 삼아 부가적 정보를 제공하는 비제한적 관계대명사 자리에는 that이 올 수 없고 which를 써야 한다. 'raises cortisol levels, that explains why'의 that을 which로 고쳐야 한다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
어법상 틀린 것을 모두 골라 기호를 쓰고 바르게 고치시오.
ⓐThis is all that the manager expects from us.
ⓑThe brush with that she painted the picture is broken.
ⓒHe is the only player that scored a goal today.
ⓓTell that you learned in class.
ⓔDid you notice the girl and her parrot that were singing on stage?
→
→
answer: ⓑ with that → with which, ⓓ Tell that → Tell what
solution: ⓑ는 관계대명사 that이 전치사 바로 뒤에 올 수 없으므로 with that을 with which로 고쳐야 한다. (The brush with which she painted the picture is broken.) ⓓ는 선행사 없이 '~하는 것'이라는 의미로 관계대명사 that을 명사절처럼 쓴 오류로, that을 what으로 고쳐야 한다. (Tell what you learned in class.) ⓐ은 all이 선행사일 때 관계대명사 that을 쓰는 것이 자연스러우므로 옳다. ⓒ은 the only가 선행사를 수식할 때 관계대명사 that을 쓰는 것이 적절하므로 옳다. ⓔ는 선행사가 사람(girl)과 동물(parrot)이 함께 있을 때 관계대명사 that을 쓰는 것이 자연스러우므로 옳다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body: 다음 문장 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: She missed the flight because of she arrived late at the airport.
Even if the exam is difficult, you should try your best.
As we plan and prepare, so will our future be shaped.
If you see a sign with a suitcase and passport, you will find a place where you can check in for your flight.
Not until the discovery of penicillin were patients given an effective treatment for infections.
solution: ④ because of he was feeling sick → because he was feeling sick because of는 전치사이므로 뒤에 명사(구)가 와야 한다. 뒤에 주어와 동사로 이루어진 절이 이어지므로 접속사 because가 알맞다. ① Even if는 ‘비록 ~일지라도’라는 양보의 접속사로 절을 이끄므로 알맞다. ② As ~, so + 동사 + 주어의 도치 구조로 알맞다. ③ where는 place를 선행사로 하며 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어지므로 알맞다. ⑤ Not until이 문두에 나오면서 주어와 동사가 도치된 구조로 알맞다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓒ 중 어법상 틀린 기호를 쓰고 바르게 고치시오.
Since 1930, the World Cup has evolved from a small international tournament into the most watched sporting event on Earth. FIFA and its member nations rotate hosting duties every four years, ⓐthat means that no single country hosts too frequently. The 2014 World Cup, ⓑin which Germany achieved a historic 7-1 victory over host nation Brazil, is remembered as one of the most dramatic matches ever. Mario Götze scored the goal ⓒthat won the tournament for Germany.
→
solution: ⓐ는 앞 절 전체인 FIFA and its member nations rotate hosting duties every four years를 받아 ‘그것은 ~을 의미한다’는 뜻을 나타내는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사이므로 that이 아니라 which를 써야 한다. ⓑ의 in which는 선행사 The 2014 World Cup을 수식하는 전치사+관계대명사 구조이고, ⓒ의 that은 선행사 the goal을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사이므로 올바르다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
Producing new plastic products from raw materials takes a heavy toll on our environment. Our current manufacturing methods cause problems with pollution, energy use, and resource depletion. But there are some creative solutions! (A)One possible solution is recycling, and it promises to make our resource use as efficient as possible. Recycling centers are built close to residential areas, ⓐwhich shortens the distance that waste must travel. This allows us to process materials quickly. Another benefit is that it creates jobs for local workers,
ⓑwhich brings economic growth to the community.

밑줄 친 ⓐ, ⓑ가 각각 가리키는 것을 찾아 우리말로 쓰시오.
ⓐ
ⓑ
answer: ⓐ 재활용 센터가 주거 지역 가까이에 지어진다는 것, ⓑ (재활 용이) 지역 노동자들에게 일자리를 창출한다는 것
solution: ⓐ와 ⓑ의 which는 특정 명사가 아니라 앞에 나온 절 전체의 내용을 선행사로 받는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사이다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
Producing new plastic products from raw materials takes a heavy toll on our environment. Our current manufacturing methods cause problems with pollution, energy use, and resource depletion. But there are some creative solutions! (A)One possible solution is recycling, and it promises to make our resource use as efficient as possible. Recycling centers are built close to residential areas, ⓐwhich shortens the distance that waste must travel. This allows us to process materials quickly. Another benefit is that it creates jobs for local workers,
ⓑwhich brings economic growth to the community.

밑줄 친 문장 (A)을 관계사를 이용하여 다시 쓰시오.
→
answer: Recycling, which promises to make our resource use as efficient as possible, is one possible solution.
solution: 두 개의 절을 접속사 and로 연결한 문장을 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which를 사용해 한 문장으로 결합한다. it은 앞의 명사 recycling을 가리키므로 콤마 뒤에 which를 써서 삽입절을 만든다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Internet addiction often begins as a result of a stressful experience. Common stressful experiences are loneliness, anxiety (A)[due to / since] exams, or dissatisfaction with real-life relationships. People who worry about being left out may be more likely to develop internet addiction. Teenagers are particularly vulnerable,
(B)[because / because of] the pressure at this time in life to stay connected and to keep up with friends online. Added to this is the pressure (C)[on / of] teenagers from social media to gain followers, to post frequently, to maintain an image and to meet peers' expectations. * internet addiction 인터넷 중독 / vulnerable (위험 등에) 노 출되어 있는
solution: (A) 뒤에 명사구(exams)가 이어지므로 전치사 due to가 적절하다. since는 뒤에 절이 와야 한다. (B) 뒤에 명사구(the pressure ~)가 이어지므로 전치사구 because of가 적절하다. because는 뒤에 절이 와야 한다. (C) 'pressure on 사람' 형태의 어구이므로 on이 적절하다. 따라서 정답은 ⑤이다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 중 어법에 맞지 않는 두 문장을 찾아 각각 틀린 부분을 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
ⓐIf the weather turns cold or stays mild affects the farmers' planting schedule.
ⓑStudents in the advanced class tend to study independently, while those in the beginner class need more guidance.
ⓒPlease call me as soon as you arrive at the airport.
ⓓDespite the negotiations failed, the two companies remained on good terms. 틀린 번호 ( ): _____ → 틀린 번호 ( ): _____ →
solution: a는 주어 역할을 하는 명사절 자리에 If를 사용했으므로 Whether로 고쳐야 한다. d는 Despite가 전치사이므로 뒤에 명사(구)가 와야 하는데 'the negotiations failed'라는 절이 이어졌으므로 접속사 Although로 고쳐야 한다. b는 while을 이용한 대조 구문이 올바르게 쓰였고, c는 as soon as를 이용한 시간 부사절이 올바르게 쓰였으므로 어법상 옳다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
The platypus is one of the most unusual mammals in the world. Its name was derived from the Greek words platus and pous, (A)[that / which] mean "flat foot," referring to its webbed feet. The platypus can detect electrical signals from prey underwater, (B)[although / despite] it doesn't have very good eyesight. Platypuses belong to a group of mammals called monotremes, and that name refers to mammals that lay eggs instead of giving birth to live young. To put it more concretely, they are egg-laying mammals (C)[like / alike] echidnas. Also, they belong to the family Ornithorhynchidae. Other than platypuses, there are no other living members of that family. *monotreme 단공류 **Ornithorhynchidae 오리너구리과
choices: that - despite - like 실전 학습 교과서 문법 정복
solution: (A) 콤마 뒤에서 앞의 명사(the Greek words platus and pous)를 계속적으로 설명하는 관계대명사 자리이므로 that이 아닌 which가 와야 한다. (B) 뒤에 '주어+동사'로 이루어진 절(it doesn't have very good eyesight)이 이어지므로 접속사 although가 필요하다. despite는 전치사로 뒤에 명사(구)가 와야 한다. (C) 뒤에 명사(echidnas)가 이어지므로 전치사 like가 적절하다. alike는 명사를 수식하는 자리에 쓰일 수 없다. 따라서 정답은 ① which - although - like이다. 미래엔(김) 3과 문법 정복 실전
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body: 다음 중 문장 전환이 바르지 않은 것은?
choices: The thing that he most desires is freedom. →What he most desires is freedom.
You can invite anyone whom you admire to the party. →You can invite whomever you admire to the party.
No matter where she hides, her dog finds her. →Wherever she hides, her dog finds her.
We entered the garden, and there we found a hidden fountain. →We entered the garden, where we found a hidden fountain.
I apologized my classmates, but they refused my apology. →I apologized my classmates, whom refused my apology.
solution: ⑤는 앞 문장의 they가 refused의 주어 역할을 하므로 목적격 whom이 아니라 주격 관계대명사 who를 써야 한다. 따라서 ‘whom refused my apology’를 ‘who refused my apology’로 고쳐야 한다. ①은 the thing that을 what으로, ②는 anyone whom을 whomever로, ③은 no matter where를 wherever로, ④는 there를 관계부사 where로 바꾼 표현으로 모두 옳다. 따라서 정답은 ⑤이다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것끼리 짝지어진 것은?
In traditional manufacturing plants, the difference in efficiency between experienced workers and new employees ⓐis closely linked to the level of hands-on training received. As manufacturing
ⓑbecomes less reliant on manual dexterity, the efficiency gap between the two groups ⓒmight expect to widen. However, this is far from being so. ⓓIt is usually the veterans who train newcomers on new machinery while the newcomers themselves struggle to keep pace.
ⓔNew automated systems having been installed, there is less need for manual dexterity. Nevertheless, the efficiency gap tends to widen
ⓕbecause of newcomers struggle with the unfamiliar technology. Thus, in the course of automation, new employees' efficiency remains
ⓖunchanged compared to veterans'.
solution: 정답은 ①이다. ⓒ '주어인 the efficiency gap'은 스스로 기대하는 행위의 주체가 아니므로 'might expect to widen'이 아니라 'might be expected to widen'과 같이 수동태로 써야 한다. ⓕ 'because of'는 전치사이므로 뒤에 명사(구)가 와야 하는데, 'newcomers struggle'이라는 주어+동사로 이루어진 절이 왔으므로 어법상 틀리다. 'because newcomers struggle'(because+절) 또는 'because of newcomers' struggle'(because of+명사)로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ는 'is closely linked'로 주어와 수 일치가 올바르다. ⓑ는 'becomes less reliant'로 현재시제와 형용사 보어가 적절하다. ⓓ는 'It is usually the veterans who train'으로 강조구문 (cleft sentence)이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ는 'New automated systems having been installed'로 완료 수동 분사구문이 적절히 쓰였다. ⓖ는 'unchanged compared'로 형용사와 분사의 결합이 자연스럽다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Octopuses have a remarkable ability to disappear into their surroundings, and they use this skill to avoid predators. So if you're an octopus, you need to blend in quickly to survive. When (A)[hiding / hidden] itself among rocks and coral, the octopus will often change its skin texture and color within seconds, matching the pattern of its environment almost perfectly. The octopus's flexible body already gives it an advantage over predators, which have a hard time spotting movement in cluttered reefs. But predators are persistent. Marine biologists who studied octopuses in aquariums reported seeing them do something quite surprising (B)[improved / to improve] their chances of escaping notice. According to these studies, as the octopus settles into a hiding spot, it sometimes flattens its body against the surface,
(C)[which / what] allows it to reduce its shadow. Apparently, the octopus minimizes its outline.
choices: hiding - to improve - what 교과서 문법 정복 실전 학습
solution: (A) 문어가 스스로 몸을 숨기는 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 hiding이 적절하다. hidden은 수동의 의미가 되어 문맥에 맞지 않는다. (B) '눈에 띄지 않을 가능성을 높이기 위해'라는 목적을 나타내는 to부정사 to improve가 적절하다. (C) 앞 문장 전체 내용을 선행사로 받는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가 적절하다. what은 선행사를 가질 수 없으므로 어법상 틀리다. 따라서 정답은 ④이다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
Resilience is a crucial quality that is necessary for overcoming adversity and achieving long-term success. Yet it is a quality ⓐthat we often underestimate in ourselves. Many books on the subject treat it as a rare gift ⓑwhich only exceptional people possess. Others describe resilience as an ability to bounce back quickly, or
ⓒ deploy 'resilience' as a synonym for 'toughness'. Without resilience we cannot recover from setbacks, we cannot maintain motivation
ⓓnor pursue our long-term goals despite obstacles. It is often regarded as an innate trait,
ⓔthat constitutes one of the most essential qualities for personal growth.
solution: 정답은 ⑤이다. ⑤의 that은 콤마 뒤에 이어지는 계속적 용법 (non-restrictive)의 관계절을 이끌고 있는데, 관계대명사 that은 계속적 용법으로 쓰일 수 없으므로 which로 고쳐야 한다. ① that은 선행사 quality를 수식하는 제한적 용법의 관계대명사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ② which는 선행사 gift를 수식하는 제한적 용법의 관계대명사로 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ deploy는 등위접속사 or로 연결된 동사 describe와 병렬 구조를 이루며 주어 Others에 맞게 동사원형으로 쓰였으므로 적절하다. ④ nor는 부정문 뒤에서 '~도 아니다'라는 의미로 cannot과 상관적으로 쓰여 적절하다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Too much frustration about slow progress can lead to fear of mistakes and a gradual decline of motivation to practice regularly. If you are gripped by doubt and a lack of patience (A)[continue / to continue] learning the instrument, you must make an attempt to change the way you view setbacks. Learn to treat every mistake as a fresh lesson that requires you to put your effort to consistent use.
(B)[Refine / Refining] your technique through daily practice may help you to overcome your current difficulties better. Do this by focusing on mastering basic skills and developing steady rhythm that builds your confidence. When you start applying your new approach, you will find the practice more satisfying, (C)[that / which] in turn will naturally have a positive impact on your musical growth.

solution: (A)는 명사 patience 뒤에서 그 내용을 나타내는 to부정사가 와야 하므로 'to continue'가 옳다. (B)는 문장의 주어 자리이므로 동명사 'Refining'이 와야 한다. (C)는 앞 절 전체를 선행사로 받는 계속적 용법이므로 which가 옳다. 따라서 정답은 ①이다. ② continue와 Refine 모두 틀린 형태이며 that도 부적절하다. ③ continue가 틀리고 that도 틀리다. ④ to continue는 맞지만 Refine이 주어 자리에 부적절하며 that도 틀리다. ⑤ to continue와 which는 맞지만 Refine이 주어 자리에 부적절하다.

She also skillfully explored light and color, contributing to the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. solution: ⓐ Bearing → Born 주절의 주어 she는 '태어난' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 분사구문이 필요하다. bear는 '낳다'라는 뜻의 타동사이므로 능동형 현재분사 Bearing은 쓸 수 없고, Being이 생략된 수동 분사구문 형태인 과거분사 Born으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓓ portraying → portrayed 주어 'the reflection of the sunlight on the blue wall'은 그림 속에서 '묘사되는' 대상이므로 수동태 'be + p.p.'가 되어야 한다. 따라서 현재분사 portraying을 과거분사 portrayed로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ to appreciate → appreciating 'aid A in B' 구문에서 in은 전치사이므로 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 한다. 전치사 뒤에 to부정사는 올 수 없으므로 to appreciate를 appreciating으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ 앞 절 'she even studied abroad in Paris' 전체를 선행사로 받는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사이므로 which가 올바르게 쓰였다. 계속적 용법에는 that을 쓸 수 없다. ⓒ 'the social pressure'의 내용을 설명하는 동격의 that절 안에서 '~해야 한다'는 의무의 의미를 나타내는 be to 용법이므로 were to가 올바르게 쓰였다.

Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. ⓐBorn in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia,
ⓑwhich she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, ⓒgenerated an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows ⓓdecorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later ⓔmaking into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art. ( ) _____ → ( ) _____ → ( ) _____ → 실전 학습
answer: ⓑ which → where, ⓒ generated → generating, ⓔ making → made
solution: ⓑ which → where 뒤에 이어지는 절 'she met her future husband, Everett Lewis'는 주어와 목적어를 모두 갖춘 완전한 절이다. 따라서 장소를 나타내는 선행사 'Digby, Nova Scotia'를 받으려면 관계대명사 which가 아니라 관계부사 where를 써야 한다. ⓒ generated → generating 분사구문의 의미상 주어는 주절의 주어 'Her artwork'이다. 작품이 독창적이고 혁신적인 스타일을 직접 만들어 낸다는 능동의 의미이고, 뒤에 목적어 'an original, innovative style'도 있다. 따라서 과거분사 generated를 현재분사 generating으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ making → made 주어 'her story'는 책과 영화로 '만들어지는' 대상이므로 수동의 의미이다. 따라서 'was later making'을 수동태 'was later made'로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ 주절의 주어 Lewis가 '태어난' 것이므로 수동의 의미이다. 따라서 과거분사로 시작하는 분사구문 Born이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓓ 소들이 '장식된' 대상이므로 명사 cows를 앞에서 수식하는 과거분사 decorated가 올바르게 쓰였다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I’m Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you’re going to meet three amazing artists who never gave up on their art, despite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly ⓐvalued. Let’s explore each artist’s life and artwork. The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life ⓑworking on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, ⓒwhich he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often
ⓓbeen used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. ⓔUsing simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he’s now considered an important figure in American folk art.
solution: ③ which → where 선행사 'the city of Montgomery, Alabama' 뒤에 오는 'he found a job in a factory'는 주어와 목적어를 모두 갖춘 완전한 절이다. 따라서 관계대명사 which는 쓸 수 없고, 장소를 나타내는 관계부사 where를 써야 한다. where는 in which로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다. 따라서 ③이 정답이다. ① 'make+목적어+목적격보어' 구문에서 목적어 'their work'는 '가치 있게 평가되는' 대상이다. 따라서 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 valued가 올바르게 쓰였다. ② 'spend+시간+-ing' 구문으로 '~하면서 시간을 보내다'라는 의미이므로 working이 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ 주어 they가 가리키는 개들은 농장에서 '이용된' 대상이다. 또한 공포를 갖게 된 시점보다 앞선 일이므로 과거완료 수동태 had been used가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⑤ 주절의 주어 Traylor가 단순한 형태와 색을 직접 '사용하는' 주체이므로, 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사로 시작하는 분사구문 Using이 올바르게 쓰였다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

If you have ever been to an art museum, you may
ⓐencounter docents and curators. While these two roles may appear similar, they actually have quite different responsibilities, requiring different skills. With the word docent ⓑcome from a Latin word meaning "to teach," docents are guides who lead museum tours and provide information about the artworks and artists ⓒfeature in an exhibition. They are usually volunteers who have a passion for art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out their responsibilities effectively, docents need ⓓspecialize training in presentation and communication skills. On the other hand, curators are professionals who design and organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming from a Latin word meaning "to take care of." Curators determine the main theme of each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme, and arrange them in an engaging way which captivates the audience. Curators are typically employed by museums and ⓔexpect / possess advanced degrees in art history, museum studies, or a related field. Despite their distinct roles, both docents and curators share a common goal: enriching every visitor's experience.
조건 1. 어형 변화 필수
2. 필요시 단어 추가 가능
3. 단어 개수에 유의하여 작성할 것.
ⓐ _____ (2단어)
ⓑ _____ (1단어)
ⓒ _____ (1단어)
ⓓ _____ (1단어)
ⓔ _____ (4단어)
실전 학습
answer: ⓐ have encountered (2단어) ⓑ coming (1단어) ⓒ featured (1단어) ⓓ specialized (1단어) ⓔ are expected to possess (4단어)
solution: ⓐ '미술관에 가본 적이 있다면(have ever been)'이라는 과거의 경험을 바탕으로 한 추측을 나타내므로, 조동사 may 뒤에 완료형인 「have + 과거분사」를 써서 '~마주쳤을지도 모른다'라는 의미를 완성하는 것이 알맞다. ⓑ 「with + 명사 + 분사」 형태의 부대상황(동시동작) 구문이다. 도슨트라는 단어가 라틴어에서 '유래하는' 능동의 의미를 지니므로 현재분사(-ing) 형태가 알맞다. ⓒ 전시회에 '다뤄지는(포함되는)' 예술가들이라는 수동의 의미로 앞에 있는 명사(artists)를 뒤에서 수식해야 하므로 과거분사 형태가 알맞다. ⓓ 뒤에 오는 명사 교육(training)을 수식하며, '전문화된'이라는 수동 및 완료의 의미를 지니므로 과거분사 형태가 알맞다. ⓔ 큐레이터들이 고학력을 '소지할 것으로(to possess) 기대된다(are expected)'는 문맥이다. 주어가 수동의 입장이므로 수동태(be expected)를 쓰고, 그 뒤에 to부정사를 연결한 형태가 알맞다. 등위접속사 and에 의해 앞의 동사(are employed)와 병렬 구조를 이루므로 be동사는 are가 된다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 have ever been과 쓰임이 다른 문장을
<보기>에서 있는 대로 고른 것은?
If you have ever been to an art museum, you may have encountered docents and curators. While these two roles may appear similar, they actually have quite different responsibilities, requiring different skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin word meaning "to teach," docents are guides who lead museum tours and provide information about the artworks and artists featured in an exhibition. They are usually volunteers who have a passion for art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized training in presentation and communication skills. On the other hand, curators are professionals who design and organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming from a Latin word meaning "to take care of." Curators determine the main theme of each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme, and arrange them in an engaging way which captivates the audience. Curators are typically employed by museums and are expected to possess advanced degrees in art history, museum studies, or a related field. Despite their distinct roles, both docents and curators share a common goal: enriching every visitor's experience.
보기 ⓐI have never seen such a beautiful sunset before.
ⓑShe has lost her passport, so she can't travel.
ⓒHave you ever tried Mexican food?
ⓓThey have already finished their homework.
ⓔHe has lived in Seoul for ten years.
ⓕI have visited that museum three times.
solution: 밑줄 친 부분은 부사 ever와 함께 쓰여 과거부터 현재까지 '~ 에 가본 적이 있다'라는 의미를 나타내는 현재완료의 경험 용법이다. ⓑ 과거에 여권을 잃어버려서 현재 가지고 있지 않다는 과거 동작의 결과를 나타내므로 쓰임이 다르다. ⓓ 부사 already(이미)와 함께 쓰여 동작이 이미 끝났음을 의미하는 완료 용법이므로 쓰임이 다르다. ⓔ 기간을 나타내는 전치사 for(~동안)와 함께 쓰여 과거부터 지금까지 동작이나 상태가 이어지는 계속 용법이므로 쓰임이 다르다. ⓐ 부사 never(결코 ~해 본 적 없다)와 함께 쓰여 과거의 경험을 나타내므로 쓰임이 같다. ⓒ 부사 ever(~해 본 적이)와 함께 쓰여 과거의 경험을 묻고 있으므로 쓰임이 같다. ⓕ 횟수를 나타내는 부사구 three times(세 번)와 함께 쓰여 과거의 경험을 나타내므로 쓰임이 같다.

choices: ⓐ: '유명한 예술가로서'라는 자격을 나타내므로 전치사 as로 고쳐야 한다.
ⓑ: 뒤에 주어, 동사, 목적어를 모두 갖춘 완전한 절이 이어지므로 목 적격 관계대명사 which로 고쳐야 한다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 옳지 않은 것끼리 짝지 은 것은?
Next, we have Maud Lewis, a ⓐrenown artist known for her heart-warming paintings. ⓑBorn in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia,
ⓒwhich she met her future husband, Everett Lewis, in. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, ⓓgenerating an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows ⓔstand in a flower field. With these features, Lewis’ paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings gradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.
solution: ⓐ renown → renowned 뒤에 오는 명사(artist)를 수식하여 '유명한 예술가'라는 뜻이 되어야 하므로, 명사형인 renown(명성)이 아니라 형용사/ 과거분사 형태인 renowned가 알맞다. ⓔ stand → standing '장식된 소들이 꽃밭에 서 있는(standing) 것을 보여준다'는 문맥이다. 앞에 쓰인 동사 shows는 지각동사나 사역동사가 아니므로 동사원형을 쓸 수 없다. 명사(decorated cows)의 상태를 보충 설명하며 능동과 진행의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 standing으로 고쳐야 알맞다. ⓑ 분사구문의 주어(Lewis)가 '태어난' 수동의 입장이므로 과거분사(Born)로 시작하는 것이 알맞다. ⓒ 선행사가 장소(Digby, Nova Scotia)일 때 보통 관계부사 where(또는 in which)를 쓰지만, 이 문장에서는 뒤에 전치사 in이 남아있으므로 전치사의 목적어 역할을 하는 목적격 관계대명사 which를 쓴 것이 문법적으로 알맞다. ⓓ generating주절의 주어(Her artwork)가 독창적인 스타일을 직접 '만들어내면서'라는 능동의 의미를 지닌 분사구문이므로 현재분사(-ing) 형태가 알맞다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ에 대한 어법 설명으로 옳지 않은것은?
Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I’m Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you’re going to meet three amazing artists ⓐwho never gave up on their art, despite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly valued. Let’s explore each artist’s life and artwork. The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, ⓑworking for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, ⓒwhere he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to
ⓓdrawing to express his life experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he’s now ⓔconsidered an important figure in American folk art.
choices: ⓐ: 선행사 artists 를 수식하며, 이어지는 절 안에서 주어 역할을 하는 주격 관계대명사이다.
ⓑ: 주절의 주어 he가 농장에서 직접 일한다는 능동의 의미 를 나타내는 분사구문이다.
ⓒ: 선행사인 장소를 부연 설명하며, 뒤에 주어와 목적어를 갖춘 완전한 절을 이끄는 계속적 용법의 관계부사이다.
ⓓ: '그림을 그리기 위하여'라는 목적의 의미를 나타내는 to 부정사의 부사적 용법으로 쓰였다.
ⓔ: 5형식 동사 consider가 수동태로 쓰여 뒤에 목적격 보 어인 명사 an important figure가 남은 형태이다.
solution: ⓓ drawing은 to부정사가 아니라 전치사 to의 목적어 역할을 하는 '동명사'이므로 설명이 틀리다. 앞에 쓰인 'turn to + 명사/동명사'는 '~에 의존하다, ~로 눈을 돌리다'라는 뜻의 숙어이다. 이때 to는 방향을 나타내는 전치사이므로 뒤에 동사원형이 아닌 동명사가 오는 것이 알맞다. ⓐ 선행사 'artists' 뒤에 바로 동사가 이어지므로 주어 역할을 하는 주격 관계대명사로 알맞다. ⓑ '주어 he'와 일하다의 관계가 직접 수행하는 능동이므로 현재분사를 사용한 분사구문으로 알맞다. ⓒ 선행사 'the city of Montgomery, Alabama'라는 장소 뒤에서 쉼표(,)와 함께 쓰였고, 뒤에 완전한 문장이 이어지므로 관계부사 where가 알맞다. ⓔ 'consider A B (A를 B로 여기다)' 구문에서 목적어(A)가 주어 자리로 나간 수동태가 되었고, 목적격 보어인 명사가 뒤에 그대로 남은 형태이므로 알맞다.
source: 영어플랫 · 미래엔(김) 공통영어2 3과 문법 정복 실전

If you have ever been to an art museum, you may have encountered docents and curators. While these two roles may ⓐappear similar, they actually have quite different responsibilities, requiring different skills. With the word docent coming from a Latin word meaning "to teach," docents are guides ⓑwho lead museum tours and provide information about the artworks and artists ⓒfeatured in an exhibition. They are usually volunteers who have a passion for art and enjoy sharing their knowledge. To carry out their responsibilities effectively, docents need specialized training in presentation and communication skills. On the other hand, curators are professionals who design and organize exhibitions, with the word curator coming from a Latin word meaning "to take care of." Curators determine the main theme of each exhibition, select artworks that fit with the theme, and arrange them in an engaging way ⓓwhich captivates the audience. Curators are typically
ⓔemploying by museums and are expected to possess advanced degrees in art history, museum studies, or a related field. Despite their distinct roles, both docents and curators share a common goal: enriching every visitor's experience.

Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist
ⓐknown for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This limited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia,
ⓑwhere she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis continued to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, ⓒgenerating an original, innovative style. Although her physical limitations
ⓓconfining her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both limitless. In Red Sleigh, red maple leaves appear on a special winter landscape, and Pair of Oxen shows decorated cows standing in a flower field. With these features, Lewis' paintings create a magical quality, like that of a fairy tale. As her paintings
ⓔgradually gained popularity, her story inspired many people and was later made into books and movies. Maud Lewis expressed her love for the world through her paintings and became an iconic figure in Canadian folk art.

Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I'm Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you're going to meet three amazing artists who never gave up on their art, ⓐdespite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly valued. Let's explore each artist's life and artwork. 실전 학습 The first artist we're going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S.
in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial discrimination, ⓑworked for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, ⓒwhere he found a job in a factory. It wasn't until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we're going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs ⓓis expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor ⓔ capturing complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he's now considered an important figure in American folk art. , _____ → , _____ →
solution: ⓑ worked → working 'he still had to face racial discrimination' 뒤에 이어지는 구조로, 주어(he)가 저임금으로 일하는 상황을 동시에 나타내는 분사구문이 필요하다. 주어 he가 능동적으로 일하는 것이므로 현재분사 working을 써야 한다. 과거형 동사 worked를 쓰면 문장에 두 개의 정동사(had, worked)가 접속사 없이 병렬되어 문법적으로 옳지 않다. ⓔ capturing → captured 'Using simple shapes and colors' 다음에 오는 주절의 동사 자리이다. 주어 Traylor에 대한 서술어가 필요하므로 정동사 형태인 captured가 와야 한다. 현재분사 capturing을 쓰면 주절에 정동사가 없게 되어 문장이 성립하지 않는다. ⓐ despite는 전치사로, 뒤에 명사구 'challenges in their lives'를 취하고 있으므로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ where는 선행사 'the city of Montgomery, Alabama'를 받아 장소를 나타내는 관계부사로, 뒤에 완전한 절('he found a job in a factory')이 이어지므로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓓ 'His fear of dogs'가 주어이고, 두려움이 그림 속에 표현되는 것이므로 수동태 is expressed가 올바르게 쓰였다.

Now let's take a look at the final artist of this exhibition: Anna Ancher, a famous painter from Denmark. When observing her paintings, you may notice a common theme─they all feature female figures. Born in Skagen, Denmark, in 1859, she later moved to Copenhagen ⓐto attend a private painting school. After that, she even studied abroad in Paris, which was unusual for women at the time. Thanks to her mother's encouragement, she was able to take advantage of these opportunities. Even after getting married, Ancher persisted in painting, objecting to the social pressure ⓑthat married women were to solely focus on household duties. Ancher differed from other artists of that era, ⓒwho depicted women as still life subjects. In contrast, she showcased them as active participants in everyday tasks, as seen in her works The Maid in the Kitchen and Sewing Fisherman's Wife. She also skillfully explored light and color,
ⓓcontributed to the rich Impressionist movement in Denmark. In her painting Sunlight in the Blue Room, the reflection of the sunlight on the blue wall is stunningly ⓔportrayed. Ancher challenged the conventional roles of women in the 20th century and displayed her exceptional artistic talent. Her paintings continue to amaze us to this day.

From Shadows to Spotlights Welcome to the Dream Art Gallery! I’m Isabel Williams, the docent for the From Shadows to Spotlights exhibit. Today, you’re going to meet three amazing artists who never gave up on their art, despite challenges in their lives. Each artist has a unique painting style and story that has made their work highly ⓐvalued. Let’s explore each artist’s life and artwork. The first artist we’re going to examine is Bill Traylor. Traylor was born into slavery in the U.S. in 1853 and spent his early life working on a cotton farm in Alabama. Although he became a free man after the American Civil War, he still had to face racial ⓑdiscrimination, working for very low wages on the farm. Later, when he was around 70 years old, Traylor moved to the city of Montgomery, Alabama, where he found a job in a factory. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to ⓒconceal his life experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. Traylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the ⓓoppressed lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. Using simple shapes and colors, Traylor captured complex moments in American history from slavery to freedom. As a result, he’s now considered an ⓔimportant figure in American folk art.

Next, we have Maud Lewis, a renowned artist known for her heart-warming paintings. Born in a small Canadian town in 1903, Lewis suffered from physical weaknesses such as distorted shoulders and fingers. This ⓐlimited her mobility and caused her to drop out of school. To make a living, she began to paint and sell Christmas cards. When her parents passed away, Lewis went to live with her aunt in Digby, Nova Scotia, where she met her future husband, Everett Lewis. After marrying, the couple spent the rest of their lives there, and Lewis ⓑceased to paint. She often depicted the Digby landscapes in paintings such as Edge of Digby Harbor. Her artwork used a mixture of bright and vivid oil paints and simple forms, generating an original, ⓒinnovative style. Although her physical limitations confined her to a small cottage, her talent and imagination were both ⓓlimitless. It wasn’t until he was 85 years old and became too ill to work that he turned to drawing to express his life experiences. Now, we’re going to look at some of his paintings, starting with Mean Dog and Man and Large Dog. ⓓTraylor had a strong fear of dogs because they had often been used on farms to watch and hunt slaves. His fear of dogs is expressed strongly in these pieces. In contrast, Woman with Purse and Man with Umbrella portrays the free lives of African Americans that he observed on the streets of Montgomery. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Neuroscience has a long history of exploring treatments for disorders of the nervous system, including the brain and spinal cord. Traditionally, researchers have studied various functions of neural implants, which are medical devices like computer chips that can be implanted in the nervous system. But here's the exciting part: with the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), researchers have begun to integrate AI into neural implants. In this post, we'll examine the incredible benefits of AI-powered neural implants, their amazing potential for the future, and the ethical concerns surrounding them. First, let's explore how this fascinating technology has been applied. The AI-powered neural implant has shown great promise in medical applications, offering solutions to a range of problems. For instance, neural implants are used to treat brain disorders like Parkinson's disease. These implants electrically stimulate targeted regions of the brain at the right time with the help of AI to restore normal brain activity. In addition, paralyzed people can have the ability to walk again with the help of a "digital bridge" between two implants inserted into their brain and spine. When they think about moving their legs, the AI analyzes the brain signals and sends them to their legs through the implants. Similarly, those who have lost their arms can use artificial arms operated by the same mechanism.
choices: AI-Powered Neural Implants: Benefits and Ethical Concerns
The History of Neuroscience and Brain Disorders
How Parkinson's Disease Damages the Nervous System
Neural Implants: A Threat to Human Privacy
The Development of Artificial Arms for Paralyzed People 1회차 실전 모의고사

다음글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
Before we can fully embrace the era of Al- powered neural implants, many tricky ethical issues should be addressed. The integration of AI technology with the human brain raises concerns about what it means to be human. Our brains are believed to be central to our identity, existence, and value as human beings. However, an over- reliance on technology may delay our natural development and create confusion about whether we are human, Al, or something in between. There's a risk that organizations or hackers could access personal data without permission through Al-connected implants. This means that our thoughts, emotions, and behaviors could be controlled by hackers. There's an additional risk that this technology could lead to even greater social inequality, given that it may not be available to all due to its high cost. Such unequal access to the technology could intensify the division between those who can afford the implants and those who cannot. I hope that we can overcome these challenges through careful consideration of neuroethics. This field highlights the social aspects of neural technology and provides possible answers to what should be considered legal and ethical. I think it is important to establish a prior review process and thoroughly assess the ethical aspects before any kind of brain research is conducted. This will ensure that science and technology progress in accordance with ethical principles.

Neuroscience has a long history of exploring treatments for disorders of the nervous system, including the brain and spinal cord. Traditionally, researchers have studied various functions of neural implants, which are medical devices like computer chips that can be implanted in the nervous system. But here's the exciting part: with the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), researchers have begun to integrate AI into neural implants. In this post, we'll examine the incredible benefits of AI-powered neural implants, their amazing potential for the future, and the ethical concerns surrounding them. First, let's explore how this fascinating technology has been applied. The AI-powered neural implant has shown great promise in medical applications, offering solutions to a range of problems. For instance, neural implants are used to treat brain disorders like Parkinson's disease. These implants electrically stimulate targeted regions of the brain at the right time with the help of AI to restore normal brain activity. In addition, paralyzed people can have the ability to walk again with the help of a "digital bridge" between two implants inserted into their brain and spine. When they think about moving their legs, the AI analyzes the brain signals and sends them to their legs through the implants. Similarly, those who have lost their arms can use artificial arms operated by .

solution: (A) 앞 문장에서 이식 장치가 일상생활을 변화시킬 것이라고 예측한 후, 바로 뒤 문장부터 생각을 읽어 게임이나 소셜 미디어를 한다는 구체적인 '예시'가 제시되므로 For example(예를 들어)이 알맞다. (B) 앞서 마음을 읽는 기능과 기억력 향상 기능 두 가지를 설명한 후, '마지막으로' 뇌의 작동 방식 자체를 혁신할 것이라는 결론적이고 추가적인 내용을 이끌어내므로 Finally(마침내, 마지막으로)가 알맞다. (C) 뒤에 명사(동명사) 형태인 'simply memorizing information(단순히 정보를 암기하는 것)'이 오고, 콤마(,) 뒤의 주절(우리는 지식을 다운로드할 수 있을 것이다)과 대조되는 '대체/부정'의 의미가 되어야 하므로 '~하는 것 대신에'를 뜻하는 전치사구 Instead of가 문법적, 논리적으로 완벽하게 알맞다. 따라서 정답은 ①이 가장 알맞다.

조건 1. 명사절 접속사(that)를 사용할 것
2. (think, necessary, strictly enforce, privacy laws, to protect, the personal information, of individuals)를 모두 포함할 것
3. 주어진 단어를 모두 활용할 것
→
answer: I think that it is necessary to strictly enforce privacy laws to protect the personal information of individuals.
solution: ~라고 생각한다'는 표현은 'I think'로 시작하며, 이어지는 내용을 명사절로 연결하는 접속사 'that'을 학생 스스로 추가해야 한다. 명사절 안에서는 'it is necessary to부정사' 구문을 사용하여 '~하는 것이 필요하다'를 표현한다. 박스에 제공된 'strictly enforce'는 to부정사의 동사원형 자리에 그대로 사용하고, 'to protect the personal information of individuals'를 뒤에 연결하여 목적을 나타낸다. 완성된 문장은 I think that it is necessary to strictly enforce privacy laws to protect the personal information of individuals.이다.

This technological integration enables users to make complex movements and control their artificial limbs with their thoughts. These advancements empower people with limb loss, giving them the freedom and opportunity to lead better lives.

Before we can fully embrace the era of AI-powered neural implants, many tricky ethical issues should be addressed. As the silicon seed takes root in our minds, the defining borders of our own reflection begin to blur. Our brains are believed to be central to our identity, existence, and value as human beings. However, an over-reliance on technology may delay our natural development and create confusion about whether we are human, AI, or something in between. Another critical issue is privacy. There’s a risk that organizations or hackers could access personal data without permission through AI-connected implants. This means that our thoughts, emotions, and behaviors could be controlled by hackers. There’s an additional risk that this technology could lead to even greater social inequality, given that it may not be available to all due to its high cost. Such unequal access to the technology could intensify the division between those who can afford the implants and those who cannot. I hope that we can overcome these challenges through careful consideration of neuroethics. This field highlights the social aspects of neural technology and provides possible answers to what should be considered legal and ethical. I think it is important to establish a prior review process and thoroughly assess the ethical aspects before any kind of brain research is conducted. This will ensure that science and technology progress in accordance with ethical principles. What do you think about this technology? Please share your opinion in the comments section below.
choices: Neuroethics is a field that seeks to resolve legal and ethical dilemmas in neural technology.
AI neural implants might cause humans to lose their clear identity as human beings.
Hackers can manipulate a person's behavior by exploiting vulnerabilities in AI implants.
Brain research should be conducted freely without any preliminary ethical assessments.
The high price of the technology could worsen the gap between the rich and the poor. 2회차 실전 모의고사

Some futurists predict that these implants will become commercially available in the next 20 to 30 years and significantly change our daily lives. For example, advances in neural implant technology will make it possible to install in our brains software that can read our minds. This could enable us to play games, type social media messages, and stream music simply by thinking. There is also great potential for memory-enhancing brain implants, similar to computer memory chips. Such devices would allow us to capture and enhance memories, and even upload and download them using the digital cloud. We could look through our memories like a social media feed, vividly recall our favorite life moments, share memories with others, and back up our most valuable memories. Finally, AI- powered neural implants would revolutionize the way our brains work. The role of the brain would shift from learning and storing information to processing the vast amounts of data provided by the implants. Instead of simply memorizing information, we would be able to download knowledge, use our creativity to interpret it, and generate new ideas.

body:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
Before we can fully embrace the era of AI-powered neural implants, many tricky ethical issues should be addressed. As the silicon seed takes root in our minds, the defining borders of our own reflection begin to blur. Our brains are believed to be central to our identity, existence, and value as human beings. However, an over-reliance on technology may delay our natural development and create confusion about whether we are human, AI, or something in between.
(A) I hope that we can overcome these challenges through careful consideration of neuroethics. This field highlights the social aspects of neural technology and provides possible answers to what should be considered legal and ethical. I think it is important to establish a prior review process and thoroughly assess the ethical aspects before any kind of brain research is conducted.
(B) There’s an additional risk that this technology could lead to even greater social inequality, given that it may not be available to all due to its high cost. Such unequal access to the technology could intensify the division between those who can afford the implants and those who cannot.
(C) Another critical issue is privacy. There’s a risk that organizations or hackers could access personal data without permission through AI- connected implants. This means that our thoughts, emotions, and behaviors could be controlled by hackers.
solution: 주어진 글에서 AI 신경 이식 장치의 시대를 수용하기 전에 해결해야 할 윤리적 문제들을 언급하며, 첫 번째 문제로 정체성의 혼란(인간과 AI의 모호한 경계)을 제시하고 있다. (C) 그 다음으로 '또 다른 중요한 문제(Another critical issue)'라는 명시적인 연결 고리를 통해 두 번째 윤리적 문제인 해커들에 의한 사생활 침해와 통제 위험을 설명하는 (C)가 이어져야 한다. (B) 이어서 '추가적인 위험(an additional risk)'이라는 표현을 사용하여 높은 비용으로 인한 사회적 불평등 심화라는 세 번째 문제를 제시하는 (B)가 오는 것이 논리적이다. (A) 마지막으로 앞서 열거된 정체성 혼란, 사생활 침해, 사회적 불평등 문제들을 '이러한 과제들(these challenges)'이라는 지시어로 받아, 신경윤리학을 통해 이를 극복하자는 결론을 내리는 (A)가 와야 한다. 따라서 가장 적절한 글의 순서는 (C) - (B) - (A)이다.

The success of AI-powered neural implants in health care is also expected to spread to other industries. Some futurists predict that these implants will become ⓐcommercial available in the next 20 to 30 years and significantly change our daily lives. For example, advances in neural implant technology will make it possible ⓑto installing in our brains software that can read our minds. This could enable us to play games, type social media messages, and stream music simply by thinking. There is also great potential for memory-enhancing brain implants, ⓒsimilar to computer memory chips. Such devices would allow us to capture and enhance memories, and even upload and download them using the digital cloud. We could look through our memories like a social media feed, vividly recall our favorite life moments, share memories with others, and back up our most valuable memories. The role of the brain would shift from learning and storing information to processing the vast amounts of data ⓓproviding by the implants. Instead of simply ⓔmemorize information, we would be able to download knowledge, use our creativity to interpret it, and generate new ideas. 2회차 실전 모의고사
solution: ③ ⓒ "similar to computer memory chips"에서 similar는 형용사로, 전치사 to와 함께 쓰이는 고정 표현 (similar to)이다. 학생들이 부사 similarly로 써야 한다고 착각하기 쉽지만, 이 문장에서 similar는 앞의 명사구 (memory-enhancing brain implants)를 서술적으로 수식하는 형용사로 쓰여 어법상 옳다. 따라서 ③이 정답이다. ① commercial → commercially "become commercially available"에서 available은 형용사이므로, 이를 수식하는 것은 부사여야 한다. commercial은 형용사이므로 형용사인 available을 수식할 수 없다. 부사 commercially로 고쳐야 한다. ② to installing → to install "make it possible to-V" 구문에서 it은 가목적어이고 진목적어는 to부정사이다. 따라서 installing(동명사)이 아닌 동사원형 install이 와야 하므로 to install로 고쳐야 한다. ④ providing → provided "the vast amounts of data"는 implants에 의해 제공되는 대상이므로, 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 provided가 와야 한다. 능동의 현재분사 providing은 어법상 틀렸다. ⑤ memorize → memorizing 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 한다. "Instead of" 다음에는 동명사 memorizing이 와야 하므로, 동사원형 memorize는 어법상 틀렸다.

First, let’s explore how this fascinating technology has been applied. The AI-powered neural implant has shown great promise in medical applications, offering solutions to a range of problems. For instance, neural implants are used to treat brain disorders like Parkinson’s disease. These implants electrically stimulate targeted regions of the brain at the right time with the help of AI to restore normal brain activity. In addition, paralyzed people can have the ability to walk again with the help of a “digital bridge” between two implants inserted into their brain and spine. When they think about moving their legs, the AI analyzes the brain signals and sends them to their legs through the implants. Similarly, those who have lost their arms can use artificial arms operated by the same mechanism.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 추론 가능한 것은?
Before we can fully embrace the era of AI- powered neural implants, many tricky ethical issues should be addressed. As the silicon seed takes root in our minds, the defining borders of our own reflection begin to blur. Our brains are believed to be central to our identity, existence, and value as human beings. However, an over- reliance on technology may delay our natural development and create confusion about whether we are human, AI, or something in between. Another critical issue is privacy. There’s a risk that organizations or hackers could access personal data without permission through AI- connected implants. This means that our thoughts, emotions, and behaviors could be controlled by hackers. There’s an additional risk that this technology could lead to even greater social inequality, given that it may not be available to all due to its high cost. Such unequal access to the technology could intensify the division between those who can afford the implants and those who cannot. I hope that we can overcome these challenges through careful consideration of neuroethics. This field highlights the social aspects of neural technology and provides possible answers to what should be considered legal and ethical. I think it is important to establish a prior review process and thoroughly assess the ethical aspects before any kind of brain research is conducted. This will ensure that science and technology progress in accordance with ethical principles. What do you think about this technology? Please share your opinion in the comments section below.
choices: Establishing a prior review process can help prevent the unethical use of brain research.
The government will soon provide AI neural implants to all citizens for free.
Hackers have already succeeded in controlling human emotions through neuroethics.

다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
Before we can fully embrace the era of AI- powered neural implants, many tricky ethical issues should be addressed. As the silicon seed takes root in our minds, the defining borders of our own reflection begin to blur. Our brains are believed to be central to our identity, existence, and value as human beings. However, an over- reliance on technology may delay our natural development and create confusion about whether we are human, AI, or something in between. Another critical issue is privacy. There’s a risk that organizations or hackers could access personal data without permission through AI- connected implants. This means that our thoughts, emotions, and behaviors could be controlled by hackers. There’s an additional risk that this technology could lead to even greater social inequality, given that it may not be available to all due to its high cost. Such unequal access to the technology could intensify the division between those who can afford the implants and those who cannot. I hope that we can overcome these challenges through careful consideration of neuroethics. This field highlights the social aspects of neural technology and provides possible answers to what should be considered legal and ethical. I think it is important to establish a prior review process and thoroughly assess the ethical aspects before any kind of brain research is conducted. This will ensure that science and technology progress in accordance with ethical principles. What do you think about this technology? Please share your opinion in the comments section below.
choices: We should carefully review the ethical aspects of AI neural implants through neuroethics.
Scientists must focus strictly on reducing the manufacturing costs of neural implants.
AI technology will naturally solve social inequality problems in the near future.
Human identity can only be preserved by strictly banning all neural technologies.
The primary goal of neuroethics is to protect the intellectual property of scientists. 3회차 실전 모의고사
solution: ① 이 글은 AI 신경 이식 장치가 정체성, 사생활, 불평등과 같은 심각한 윤리적 문제들을 야기할 수 있으므로, 이를 해결하기 위해 신경윤리학을 바탕으로 신중한 사전 검토 과정을 거쳐야 한다는 내용을 다루고 있다. 따라서 ① '우리는 신경윤리학을 통해 AI 신경 이식 장치의 윤리적 측면을 신중하게 검토해야 한다'가 요지로 가장 적절하다. ② 과학자들이 이식 장치의 '제조 비용을 줄이는 데' 집중해야 한다는 것은 글의 중심 주장이 아니다. ③ 인공지능 기술이 가까운 미래에 사회적 불평등 문제를 '자연스럽게 해결할 것'이라는 내용은 기술이 불평등을 심화시킬 수 있다는 본문과 모순된다. ④ 인간의 정체성을 보존하기 위해 모든 신경 기술을 '엄격히 금지'하자는 극단적인 주장이 아닌, 제대로 검토를 하자는 내용이다. ⑤ 신경윤리학의 주된 목표가 과학자들의 '지적 재산권 보호'라는 내용은 언급되지 않았다.
